body.text: 3.3.24/.yuvatayo hi saṃsṛṣṭam abhīkṣṇa^darśanaṃ ca puruṣaṃ prathamaṃ kāmayante/ kāmayamānā api tu na^abhiyuñjata iti prāyovādaḥ/ iti bālāyām upakramāḥ//(p.211)
body.translated_text: 3.3.24. For young women first desire a man who is familiar and frequently seen. Yet even when desiring, they do not make advances — this is the general rule. Thus [ends the section on] approaches to a young girl.
3.3.25. We shall now describe those gestures and expressions.

body.text: 3.3.26/.saṃmukhaṃ taṃ tu na vīkṣate/ vīkṣitā vrīḍāṃ darśayati/ rucyam ātmano +aṅgam apadeśena prakāśayati/ pramattaṃ pracchannaṃ nāyakam atikrāntaṃ ca vīkṣate/
body.translated_text: 3.3.26. She does not look at him face to face; when looked at, she shows bashfulness. She reveals an attractive part of her body under some pretext. She watches the hero secretly, or when he is inattentive, or when he has passed by.

body.text: 3.3.27/.pṛṣṭā ca kiṃ cit sasmitam avyakta^akṣaram anavasitā^arthaṃ ca mandaṃ mandam adhomukhī kathayati/ tat^samīpe ciraṃ sthānam abhinandati/ dūre sthitā paśyatu mām iti manyamānā parijanaṃ savadana^vikāram ābhāṣate/ taṃ deśaṃ na muñcati/
body.translated_text: 3.3.27. When asked something, she replies with a slight smile, in indistinct syllables, with inconclusive meaning, slowly and with face downcast. She delights in staying near him for a long time. When standing at a distance, thinking 'let him see me,' she speaks to her attendants with a change of expression. She does not leave that place.

body.text: 3.3.28/.yat kiṃ cid dṛṣṭvā vihasitaṃ karoti/ tatra kathām avasthāna^artham anubadhnāti/ bālasya^aṅka^gatasya^āliṅganaṃ cumbanaṃ ca karoti/ paricārikāyās tilakaṃ ca racayati/ parijanānavaṣṭabhya tās tāś ca līlā darśayati/
body.translated_text: 3.3.28. She laughs at whatever little thing she sees; she prolongs the conversation there as a pretext for staying. She embraces and kisses a child sitting in her lap. She applies a decorative mark on a maidservant. She displays various playful gestures while leaning on her attendants.

body.text: 3.3.29/.tan^mitreṣu viśvasiti/ vacanaṃ ca^eṣāṃ bahu manyate karoti ca/ tat^paricārakaiḥ saha prītiṃ saṃkathāṃ dyūtam iti ca karoti/ svakarmasu ca prabhaviṣṇur iva^etān niyuñkte/ teṣu ca nāyaka^saṃkathām anyasya kathayatsv avahitā tāṃ śṛṇoti/
body.translated_text: 3.3.29. She trusts his friends and considers their words important and acts on them. She engages in friendly conversation, playing games, and the like with his attendants. She employs them in her own tasks as if she were their superior. And when they tell stories about the hero, she listens attentively to the conversation about him.

body.text:
3.3.30/.dhātreyikayā coditā nāyakasya^udavasitaṃ praviśati/ tām antarā kṛtvā tena saha dyūtaṃ krīḍām ālāpaṃ ca^āyojayitum icchati/ analaṃkṛtā darśana^pathaṃ (p.214)pariharati/ karṇa^pattram aṅgulīyakaṃ srajaṃ vā tena yācitā sadhīram eva gātrād avatārya sakhyā haste dadāti/ tena ca dattaṃ nityaṃ dhārayati/ anya^vara^saṃkathāsu viṣaṇṇā bhavati/ tat^pakṣakaiś
ca saha na saṃsṛjyata iti//(p.215) bhavataś ca^atra ślokau ---(p.215)
body.translated_text: 3.3.30. Urged by the foster-sister, she enters the hero's dwelling. Through her as intermediary, she wishes to arrange games, play, and conversation with him. Without ornaments, she avoids his sight. When he asks for her ear-ornament, ring, or garland, she slowly removes it from her body and gives it to a friend's hand. She constantly wears what he has given. When talk arises of other suitors, she becomes dejected. And she does not associate with their partisans.
3.3.31ab. Having observed these expressions and gestures imbued with feeling,
3.3.31cd. one should devise various methods for union with the girl.
3.3.32ab. A girl [is won] through childhood play, a woman established in youth through the arts,
3.3.32cd. and an affectionate [woman] should be won through the winning over of trusted persons.
3.4. Pursuit by a single man.
3.4.1. A girl who has shown her gestures and expressions should be approached through method.

body.text: 3.4.2/.dyūte krīḍanakeṣu ca vivadamānaḥ sākāram asyāḥ pāṇim avalambeta//(p.216)
body.translated_text: 3.4.2. In games and play, while disputing, one should expressively take hold of her hand.
3.4.3. And one should perform the contact-embrace and other methods of embracing as described.
3.4.4. And in the craft of leaf-cutting, one should show her a couple that indicates one's own intention.
3.4.5. Similarly, one should show other [such images] on rare occasions.

body.text: 3.4.6/.jala^krīḍāyāṃ tad^dūrato +apsu nimagnaḥ samīpam asyā gatvā spṛṣṭvā ca^enāṃ tatra^eva^unmajjet//(p.217)
body.translated_text: 3.4.6. During water-play, diving far from her, going near her, touching her, and surfacing right there.
3.4.7. And at the [festival of] new leaves and the like, the declaration of special feelings.
3.4.8. And the narration of one's own suffering without despondency.
3.4.9. And [the narration] of a dream imbued with feeling, under the pretext of [talking about] something else.
3.4.10. At a performance or a family gathering, sitting nearby. And there, touching under some pretext.
3.4.11. And pressing foot against foot, as if seeking support.
3.4.12. Then gradually touching one toe after another.
3.4.13. And with the big toe, tapping the tips of [her] nails.
3.4.14. When successful there, one should seek more than [just] the foot.
3.4.15. And for the sake of [testing her] tolerance, one should repeat the same [gesture].
3.4.16. When washing her feet, pressing her toes by gripping them between [his] toes.
3.4.17. In the giving or receiving of an object, the display of emotion directed at her.
3.4.18. And after rinsing the mouth, sprinkling with water.

body.text: 3.4.19/.vijane tamasi ca dvandvam āsīnaḥ kṣāntiṃ kruvīta/ samāna^deśa^śayyāyāṃ ca//(p.218)
body.translated_text: 3.4.19. And when seated together as a couple in a secluded place, in darkness, one should test [her] tolerance. And in a shared sleeping place.
3.4.20. There, the declaration of feelings in a meaningful way, without causing alarm.

body.text: 3.4.21/.vivikte ca kiṃ cid asti kathayitavyam ity uktvā nirvacanaṃ bhāvaṃ ca tatra^upalakṣayet/ yathā pāra^dārike vakṣyāmaḥ//(p.219)
body.translated_text: 3.4.21. And in a secluded place, having said 'there is something to be told,' one should note [her] speechlessness and feelings — as we shall describe in the section on other men's wives.

body.text:
3.4.22/.vidita^bhāvas tu vyādhim apadiśya^enāṃ vārtā^grahaṇa^arthaṃ svam udavasitam ānayet//(p.219)
3.4.23/.āgatāyāś ca śiraḥ^pīḍane niyogaḥ/ pāṇim avalambya ca^asyāḥ sākāraṃ nayanayor lalāṭe ca nidadhyāt//(p.219)
body.translated_text:
3.4.22. But one whose feelings are known should feign illness and have her brought to his own dwelling for the purpose of inquiring about his condition.
3.4.23. And when she has come, the task of pressing the head [is assigned to her]. And he should place [his hand] on her palm with feeling, placing it expressively on her eyes and forehead.
3.4.24. And under the pretext of [applying] medicine, he should direct her to perform a task on him.

body.text: 3.4.25/.idaṃ tvayā kartavyam/ na hy etad ṛte kanyayā anyena kāryam iti gacchantīṃ punar āgamana^anubandham enāṃ visṛjet//(p.220)
body.translated_text: 3.4.25. 'This must be done by you; for no other girl can do this' — and when she leaves, he should let her go with an arrangement for her return.

body.text: 3.4.26/.asya ca yogasya trirātraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ ca prayuktiḥ//(p.220)
body.translated_text: 3.4.26. And this method should be practiced over three nights and at three junctions [of the day].
3.4.27. And when she comes for the purpose of frequent visits, he should extend the conversation.

body.text: 3.4.28/.anyābhir api saha viśvāsana^artham adhikam adhikaṃ ca^abhiyuñjīta/ na tu vācā nirvadet//(p.220)
body.translated_text: 3.4.28. And to build trust, he should make advances increasingly with other [women] too. But he should not declare [his feelings] in words.

body.text: 3.4.29/.dūragata^bhāvo +api hi kanyāsu na nirvedena siddhyati^iti ghoṭakamukhaḥ//(p.220)
body.translated_text: 3.4.29. For even one whose feelings have progressed far does not succeed with girls through verbal declaration — says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
3.4.30. But when he considers her well-won, only then should he make his move.

body.text: 3.4.31/.pradoṣe niśi tamasi ca yoṣito manda^sādhvasāḥ surata^(p.220)vyavasāyinyo rāgavatyaś ca bhavanti/ na ca puruṣaṃ pratyācakṣate/ tasmāt tatkālaṃ prayojayitavyā iti prāyovādaḥ//(p.221)
body.translated_text: 3.4.31. In the early evening, at night, and in darkness, women are of mild timidity, determined on lovemaking, passionate, and do not refuse a man. Therefore, one should approach [the girl] at those times — this is the general rule.

body.text: 3.4.32/.eka^puruṣa^abhiyogānāṃ tv asaṃbhave gṛhīta^arthayā dhātreyikayā sakhyā vā tasyām antarbhūtayā tam artham anirvadantyā saha^enām aṅkam ānāyayet/ tato yathoktam abhiyuñjīta//(p.221)
body.translated_text: 3.4.32. But when the approaches of a single man are not possible, he should bring her to his lap through the nurse-maid or a female friend who has been won over and who, having taken his side, does not reveal the matter. Then he should court her as previously described.

body.text: 3.4.33/.svāṃ vā paricārikām ādāv eva sakhītvena^asyāḥ praṇidadhyāt//(p.221)
body.translated_text: 3.4.33. Or he should from the very beginning establish his own maid-servant in a position of friendship with her.

body.text: 3.4.34/.yajñe vivāhe yātrāyām utsave vyasane prekṣaṇaka^vyāpṛte jane tatra tatra ca dṛṣṭa^iṅgita^ākārāṃ parīkṣita^bhāvām ekākinīm upakrameta/
body.translated_text: 3.4.34. At a sacrifice, wedding, festival, procession, calamity, or when people are occupied with a spectacle — in each such situation, he should approach her alone, after observing her gestures and expressions and testing her feelings.

body.text: 3.4.35/.na hi dṛṣṭa^bhāvā yoṣito deśe kāle ca prayujyamānā vyāvartanta iti vātsyāyanaḥ/ ity ekapuruṣa^abhiyogāḥ/(p.221)
body.translated_text: 3.4.35. For women whose feelings have been observed do not turn away when approached at the right place and time — says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. Thus [are described] the approaches of a single man.

body.text: 3.4.36/.manda^apadeśā guṇavaty api kanyā dhana^hīnā kulīnā^api samānair ayācyāmānā mātā^pitṛ^viyuktā vā jñāti^kula^vartinī vā prāpta^yauvanā pāṇi^grahaṇaṃ svayam abhīpseta//(p.222)
body.translated_text: 3.4.36. A girl who, though virtuous, is without wealth; who, though of good family, is not sought by equals; or who is separated from her mother and father; or who lives in the house of relatives — upon reaching womanhood, should herself desire marriage.
3.4.37. She should court a man who is virtuous, capable, and handsome, through the affection natural to youth.

body.text: 3.4.38/.yaṃ vā manyeta mātā^pitror asamīkṣayā svayam apy ayam indriya^daurbalyān mayi pravartiṣyata iti priya^hita^upacārair abhīkṣṇa^saṃdarśanena ca tam āvarjayet//(p.222)
body.translated_text: 3.4.38. Or, one whom she thinks: 'this man too, through the weakness of his senses, will of his own accord be drawn to me, even without the scrutiny of mother and father' — him she should attract through agreeable and affectionate attentions and frequent meetings.

body.text: 3.4.39/.mātā ca^enāṃ sakhībhir dhātreyikābhiś ca saha tad^abhimukhīṃ kuryāt//(p.223)
body.translated_text: 3.4.39. And her mother should, through her female friends and nurse-maids, make her favorably disposed toward him.

body.text: 3.4.40/.puṣpa^gandha^tāmbūla^hastāyā vijane vikāle ca tad^upasthānam/ kalā^kauśala^prakāśane vā saṃvāhane śirasaḥ pīḍane ca^aucitya^darśanam/ prayojyasya sātmya^yuktāḥ kathā^yogāḥ bālāyām upakrameṣu yathoktam ācaret//(p.223)
body.translated_text: 3.4.40. With flowers, perfume, and betel in hand, she should attend upon him in private and at unusual hours; or display her skill in the arts, demonstrate fitness in massage and head-pressing. With the man she intends [to win], she should employ suitable conversational tactics; and with the young girl, she should proceed with the approaches as previously described.

body.text: 3.4.41/.na ca^eva^antarā^api puruṣaṃ svayam abhiyuñjīta/ svayam abhiyoginī hi yuvatiḥ saubhāgyaṃ jahāti^ity^ācāryāḥ//(p.223)
body.translated_text: 3.4.41. But she should never court the man directly herself. For the teachers say: a young woman who courts a man herself loses her good fortune.
3.4.42. But she should accept his approaches with compliance.

body.text: 3.4.43/.pariṣvaktā ca na vikṛtiṃ bhajet/ ślakṣṇam ākāram ajānatī^iva pratigṛhṇīyāt/ vadana^grahaṇe balāt kāraḥ/
body.translated_text: 3.4.43. And when embraced, she should not show agitation. She should receive [his advances] gently, as if not understanding [their] intent. When he takes her face, [she should resist] with force.
3.4.44. Being entreated for the experience of love, [she should allow] the touching of private parts only with difficulty.
3.4.45. Even when entreated, she should not herself be too revealing — except at a time when the outcome is certain.

body.text: 3.4.46/.yadā tu manyeta^anurakto mayi na vyāvartiṣyata iti tadā^eva^enam abhiyuñjānaṃ bāla^bhāva^mokṣāya *tvarayet[ch:tvaret]/
body.translated_text: 3.4.46. But when she thinks 'he is attached to me and will not turn away,' then she should urge the courting man to hasten the release from the state of maidenhood.
3.4.47. And having been released from her maiden state, she should make it known to trustworthy persons. Thus [is described] the winning over of the intended [suitor].
3.4.48a. A girl being courted should choose as her refuge

body.text: 3.4.48b/.anukūlaṃ ca vaśyaṃ ca tasya kuryāt parigraham//(p.224)
body.translated_text: 3.4.48b. one who is agreeable and amenable, and embrace him.
3.4.49a. Disregarding virtues and looking only at physical suitability,

body.text:
3.4.49b/.kurvīta dhana^lobhena patiṃ sa^apatnakeṣv api//(p.225)
3.4.50a/.tatra yukta^guṇaṃ vaśyaṃ śaktaṃ balavad arthinam/(p.225)
body.translated_text: 3.4.49b. she should not, out of greed for wealth, take a husband even among those who have co-wives. There, she should not entice one who courts [her] with proper qualities, who is amenable, capable, strong, and earnest.
3.4.50b. A girl should not entice [such a man].
3.4.51a. Better a husband who is amenable, even if poor, even if without qualities, [but] self-supporting,

body.text: 3.4.51b/.guṇair yukto +api na tv evaṃ bahu^sādhāraṇaḥ patiḥ//(p.225)
body.translated_text: 3.4.51b. than one endowed with qualities but shared among many women.
3.4.52a. For the wives of wealthy men are generally many and unrestrained;
3.4.52b. even when there is enjoyment externally, there is no trust — [they are] those whose happiness is only outward.

body.text: 3.4.53a/.nīco yas tv abhiyuñjīta puruṣaḥ palito +api vā/
body.translated_text: 3.4.53a. A man who is of low [birth] or who courts [her], or who is grey-haired,
3.4.53b. or who habitually travels to foreign lands — he does not deserve union.
3.4.54a. One who courts by chance, or one who is excessively deceitful or addicted to gambling,

body.text: 3.4.54b/.sapatnīkaś ca sa^apatyo na sa saṃyogam arhati//
body.translated_text: 3.4.54b. or who has co-wives and children — he does not deserve union.
3.4.55a. Among suitors of equal qualities, one who selects [the girl] is the best suitor;
3.4.55b. for the excellence of a suitor lies in the fact that he is motivated by love.
3.5. [Chapter on marriage arrangements]
3.5.1. When there is no opportunity for the man to meet the girl privately in the usual course of events, he should approach the nurse-maid, winning her over through affection and benefits.

body.text: 3.5.2/.sā ca^enām aviditā nāma nāyakasya bhūtvā tad^guṇair anurañjayet/ tasyāś ca rucyān nāyaka^guṇān bhūyiṣṭham upavarṇayet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.2. And she, without revealing the man's identity, should make the girl enamored of his qualities; and she should especially describe the man's qualities that would appeal to her.
3.5.3. She should set forth the faults of other suitor-fathers as contrary to [the girl's] wishes.

body.text: 3.5.4/.mātā^pitroś ca guṇān abhijñatāṃ lubdhatāṃ ca capalatāṃ ca bāndhavānām/
body.translated_text: 3.5.4. And [she should speak of] the qualities of the mother and father, as well as the knowledge, greed, and fickleness of relatives.

body.text: 3.5.5/.yāś ca^anyā api samāna^jātīyāḥ kanyāḥ śakuntalā^ādyāḥ svabuddhyā bhartāraṃ prāpya saṃprayuktā modante sma tāś ca^asyā nidarśayet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.5. And she should point out to her other girls of the same class — <s>Śakuntalā</s> and others — who, having obtained a husband of their own choosing through their own judgment, rejoice in their union.

body.text: 3.5.6/.mahā^kuleṣu sa^apatnakair bādhyāmānā *vidviṣṭā[ch:vidviṣṭāḥ] duḥkhitāḥ parityaktāś ca dṛśyante/
body.translated_text: 3.5.6. In great families, those harassed by co-wives are seen to be despised, unhappy, and abandoned.
3.5.7. And she should describe his future prospects.
3.5.8. She should describe the unimpaired happiness of being the sole wife, and the devotion of the man.

body.text: 3.5.9/.samanorathāyāś ca^asyā apāyaṃ sādhvasaṃ vrīḍāṃ ca hetubhir avacchindyāt/
body.translated_text: 3.5.9. And when [the girl] shares the same desire, [the nurse-maid] should dispel her apprehension, timidity, and modesty with [suitable] reasons.
3.5.10. And she should carry out the entire role of a female messenger.

body.text: 3.5.11/.tvām ajānatīm iva nāyako balād grahīṣyati^iti tathā suparigṛhītaṃ syād iti yojayet//(p.227)
body.translated_text: 3.5.11. She should arrange it [so that] the man would seize her as if without her knowledge, by force — so that [the arrangement] would be well-grasped.

body.text: 3.5.12/.pratipannām abhipreta^avakāśa^vartinīṃ nāyakaḥ śrotriya^āgārād agnim ānāyya kuśān āstīrya yathāsmṛti hutvā ca triḥ parikramet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.12. When the [girl] has consented and is in a suitable place, the man should bring fire from the house of a <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar), spread <s>kuśa</s> grass, and having offered oblations according to the prescribed rites, should circumambulate [the fire] three times.
3.5.13. Then he should make [the matter] known to the mother and father.

body.text: 3.5.14/.agni^sākṣikā hi vivāhā na nivartanta ity ācārya^samayaḥ//(p.228)
body.translated_text: 3.5.14. For marriages witnessed by fire are irrevocable — this is the established doctrine of the teachers.
3.5.15. And having deflowered her, he should gradually make it known to her family.

body.text: 3.5.16/.tad^bāndhavāś ca yathā kulasya^adhaṃ pariharanto daṇḍa^bhayāc ca tasmā eva^enāṃ dadyus tathā yojayet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.16. And he should arrange things so that her relatives, avoiding disgrace to the family and out of fear of punishment, would give her to him.

body.text: 3.5.17/.anantaraṃ ca prīty^upagraheṇa rāgeṇa tad^bāndhavān prīṇayed iti/
body.translated_text: 3.5.17. And afterward, he should gratify her relatives through affectionate hospitality and through love.
3.5.18. Or he should endeavor through the <s>Gāndharva</s> form of marriage.

body.text: 3.5.19/.apratipadyamānāyām antaś cāriṇīm anyāṃ kula^pramadāṃ pūrva^saṃsṛṣṭāṃ prīyamāṇāṃ ca^upagṛhya tayā saha viṣahyam avakāśam enām anya^kārya^apadeśena^ānayayet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.19. When she does not consent, having won over another respectable lady who moves freely within [the household], who was previously acquainted and is well-disposed, he should bring her [the girl], on some other pretext, to a place accessible to him, together with that [lady].
3.5.20. Then, bringing fire from a <s>Śrotriya</s>'s house — [the rest is] the same as before.

body.text: 3.5.21/.āsanne ca vivāhe mātaram asyās tad abhimata^doṣair anuśayaṃ grāhayet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.21. And when a [different] marriage is imminent, he should make her mother feel regret through [exposing] the faults of the favored [suitor].

body.text: 3.5.22/.tatas tad^anumatena prātiveśya^abhavane niśi nāyakam ānāyya śrotriya^āgārād agnim iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa//(p.229)
body.translated_text: 3.5.22. Then, with her consent, at night, at a neighbor's house, bringing the man — then bringing fire from a <s>Śrotriya</s>'s house — [the rest is] the same as before.

body.text: 3.5.23/.bhrātaram asyā vā samāna^vayasaṃ veśyāsu parastrīṣu vā prasaktam asukareṇa sāhāya^dānena priya^upagrahaiś ca sudīrgha^kālam anurañjayet/ ante ca sva^abhiprāyaṃ grāhayet/
body.translated_text: 3.5.23. Or, he should long cultivate her brother — of the same age, attached to courtesans or other men's wives — through difficult favors, affectionate gifts, and over a very long period. And at the end, he should make him understand his intention.

body.text: 3.5.24/.prāyeṇa hi yuvānaḥ samāna^śīla^vyasana^vayasāṃ vayasyānām arthe jīvitam api tyajanti/ tatas tena^eva^anyakāryāt tām ānāyayet/ viṣahyaṃ sā^avakāśam iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa//(p.230)
body.translated_text: 3.5.24. For young men generally would give up even their life for the sake of friends who share the same disposition, vice, and age. Then through that very [brother], under some other pretext, he should bring her [to the accessible place] — [the rest is] the same as before.

body.text: 3.5.25/.aṣṭamī^candrika^ādiṣu ca dhātreyikā madanīyam enāṃ pāyayitvā kiṃ cid ātmanaḥ kāryam uddiśya nāyakasya viṣahyaṃ deśam ānayet/ tatra^enāṃ madāt saṃjñām apratipadyamānāṃ dūṣayitvā^iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa//(p.230)
body.translated_text: 3.5.25. And on the eighth-day festival, moonlit nights, and the like, the nurse-maid, having made [the girl] drink an intoxicating beverage, citing some task of her own, should bring her to a place accessible to the man. There, having deflowered her while she, due to intoxication, does not recognize [what is happening] — [the rest is] the same as before.

body.text: 3.5.26/.suptāṃ ca^ekacāriṇīṃ dhātreyikāṃ vārayitvā saṃjñām apratipadyamānāṃ dūṣayitvā^iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa//(p.230)
body.translated_text: 3.5.26. And having isolated the sleeping [girl] from the nurse-maid, having deflowered her while she does not recognize [what is happening] — [the rest is] the same as before.

body.text: 3.5.27/.grāma^antaram udyānaṃ vā gacchantīṃ viditvā susaṃbhṛta^sahāyo nāyakas tadā rakṣiṇo vitrāsya hatvā vā kanyām apaharet/ iti vivāha^yogāḥ//(p.231)
body.translated_text: 3.5.27. And learning that she is going to a neighboring village or garden, the man, with well-equipped companions, should at that time frighten or kill the guards and abduct the girl. Thus [are described] the methods of marriage.

body.text: 3.5.28a/.pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ pradhānaṃ syād vivāho dharmataḥ sthiteḥ/(p.231)
body.translated_text: 3.5.28a. Each preceding [form of] marriage should be considered more important, from the standpoint of <s>dharma</s>;

body.text: 3.5.28b/.pūrva^abhāve tataḥ kāryo yo ya uttara uttaraḥ//(p.231)
body.translated_text: 3.5.28b. in the absence of the preceding, each successive one should then be undertaken.
3.5.29a. Since the result of accomplished marriages is mutual love,
3.5.29b. even though middling, the <s>Gāndharva</s> [marriage] is honored because of the good union [it creates].
3.5.30a. Because of its pleasantness, its lack of much trouble, and its absence of obstacles,
3.5.30b. and because it is rooted in mutual love, the <s>Gāndharva</s> [marriage] is considered the best.
4. Section on the Wife (<s>bhāryādhikārika</s>).
4.1. Conduct of the Sole Wife and Behavior During the Husband's Absence.
4.1.1. A wife who is the sole [wife] should, with deep and intimate trust, conduct herself toward her husband as toward a god, with compliance.
4.1.2. With his approval, she should take upon herself the care of the household.

body.text: 4.1.3/.veśma ca śuci susaṃmṛṣṭa^sthānaṃ viracita^vividha^kusumaṃ ślakṣṇa^bhūmi^talaṃ hṛdya^darśanaṃ triṣavaṇa^ācarita^bali^karma pūjita^deva^āyatanaṃ kuryāt//(p.233)
body.translated_text: 4.1.3. She should keep the house clean, with well-swept areas, adorned with various flowers, with a smooth floor, pleasant to behold, with the offering ritual (<s>balikarma</s>) performed at the three junctures [of the day], and with the temple of the household deity properly worshipped.
4.1.4. For there is nothing else that captures the hearts of householders more than this — says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

body.text: 4.1.5/.guruṣu bhṛtya^vargeṣu nāyaka^bhaginīṣu tat^patiṣu ca yathā^arhaṃ pratipattiḥ//(p.234)
body.translated_text: 4.1.5. Toward elders, the retinue of servants, the husband's sisters, and their husbands, she should behave with appropriate respect.
4.1.6. And in the kitchen gardens, she should grow beds of green vegetables, clumps of sugar-cane, cumin, mustard, celery, fennel, bay-leaf bushes, and the like.

body.text: 4.1.7/.kubjaka^āmalaka^mallikā^jātī^kuraṇṭaka^navamālikā^tagara^nandyāvarta^j apā^gulmān anyāṃś ca bahu^puṣpān bālaka^uśīraka^pātālikāṃś ca vṛkṣa^vāṭikāyāṃ ca sthaṇḍilāni manojñāni kārayet//(p.234)
body.translated_text: 4.1.7. In the tree-garden, she should plant jasmine, emblic myrhobalan, <s>mallikā</s>, Arabian jasmine, <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>, <s>navamālikā</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, hibiscus bushes, and other profusely flowering [plants], as well as <s>bālaka</s> [fragrant grass], <s>uśīra</s> [vetiver], and trumpet-flower trees, and [she should create] charming platforms.
4.1.8. In the center, she should have a well, a reservoir, or a pond dug.
4.1.9. She should not associate with female mendicants, female ascetics, female <s>Jain</s> nuns, unchaste women, deceivers, fortune-tellers, or practitioners of root-magic.

body.text: 4.1.10/.bhojane ca rucitam idam asmai dveṣyam idaṃ pathyam idam apathyam idam iti ca vindyāt//(p.235)
body.translated_text: 4.1.10. And regarding food, she should know: 'this he likes, this he dislikes, this is wholesome for him, and this is unwholesome.'

body.text: 4.1.11/.svaraṃ bahir upaśrutya bhavanam āgacchataḥ kiṃ kṛtyam iti bruvatī sajjā bhavana^madhye tiṣṭhet//(p.235)
body.translated_text: 4.1.11. Upon hearing his voice from outside, of [him] coming home, she, saying 'what is to be done?' should stand ready in the interior of the house.
4.1.12. Having dismissed the maid-servant, she should herself wash [his] feet.

body.text: 4.1.13/.nāyakasya ca na vimukta^bhūṣaṇaṃ vijane saṃdarśane tiṣṭhet//(p.235)
body.translated_text: 4.1.13. And she should not stand before the husband without ornaments in a private viewing.
4.1.14. She should privately advise [him] against excessive or improper expenditure.

body.text: 4.1.15/.āvāhe vivāhe yajñe gamanaṃ sakhībhiḥ saha goṣṭhīṃ devatā^abhigamanam ity anujñātā kuryāt//(p.235)
body.translated_text: 4.1.15. At wedding receptions, marriages, and sacrifices, going [out] with female friends, attending social gatherings, and visiting temples — she should do [these] only with [his] permission.
4.1.16. And in all amusements, [her] engagement should be in conformity with him.

body.text: 4.1.17/.paścāt saṃveśanaṃ pūrvam utthānam anavabodhanaṃ ca suptasya//(p.236)
body.translated_text: 4.1.17. Going to bed after [him] and rising before [him], and not waking him when he is asleep.
4.1.18. And the kitchen should be well-protected and also presentable.
4.1.19. When the husband commits offenses, she, though somewhat displeased, should not excessively censure [him].

body.text: 4.1.20/.sādhikṣepa^vacanaṃ tv enaṃ mitra^jana^madhyastham ekākinaṃ vā^apy upālabheta/ na ca mūla^kārikā syāt//(p.236)
body.translated_text: 4.1.20. But she may reproach him with words mixed with gentle rebuke, either among friends or when alone — and she should not practice root-magic.
4.1.21. For there is nothing else that causes distrust more than this — says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

body.text: 4.1.22/.durvyāhṛtaṃ durnirīkṣitam anyato mantraṇaṃ dvāra^deśa^avasthānaṃ nirīkṣaṇaṃ vā niṣkuṭeṣu mantraṇaṃ vivikteṣu ciram avasthānam iti varjayet//(p.236)
body.translated_text: 4.1.22. She should avoid improper speech, improper looks, consulting with another, standing at the doorway or looking [out], consulting in gardens, and lingering long in secluded places.
4.1.23. And she should be aware of sweat, dental stains, and bad odors — these are the causes of repulsion.

body.text: 4.1.24/.bahu^bhūṣaṇaṃ vividha^kusuma^anulepanaṃ vividha^aṅga^rāga^samujjvalaṃ vāsa ity ābhigāmiko veṣaḥ/
body.translated_text: 4.1.24. Abundant ornaments, various flower-garlands and ointments, clothing resplendent with various body-paints — this is the attire for attracting (<s>ābhigāmika</s>).

body.text: 4.1.25/.pratanu^ślakṣṇa^alpa^dukūlatā parimitam ābharaṇaṃ sugandhitā na^atyulbaṇam anulepanam/ tathā śuklāny anyāni puṣpāṇi^iti vaihāriko veṣaḥ//(p.237)
body.translated_text: 4.1.25. Thin, smooth, and scanty silk garments, limited jewelry, fragrance not excessively strong in ointment, and other white flowers — this is the attire for enjoyment (<s>vaihārika</s>).

body.text: 4.1.26/.nāyakasya vratam upavāsaṃ ca svayam api karaṇena^anuvarteta/ vāritāyāṃ ca na^aham atra nirbandhanīya^iti tad^vacaso nivartanam//(p.237)
body.translated_text: 4.1.26. She should observe the lover's vows and fasts by performing them herself. And when forbidden [by him], she should desist from his words, [saying] 'I should not be compelled in this.'
4.1.27. And at the proper time, the acquisition at fair prices of vessels of clay, split-bamboo, wood, leather, and metal.

body.text: 4.1.28/.tathā lavaṇa^snehayoś ca gandha^dravya^kaṭuka^bhāṇḍa^oṣadhānāṃ ca durlabhānāṃ bhavanesu pracchannaṃ nidhānam//(p.237)
body.translated_text: 4.1.28. Likewise, the secret storage in the house of salt, oils, fragrant substances, pungent preparations, and rare medicines.

body.text: 4.1.29/.mūlaka^āluka^pālaṅkī damanaka^āmrātaka^ervāruka^trapusa^vārtāka^kūṣmāṇḍa^ālābu^sūraṇa^śukanāsā ^svayaṃguptā^tilaparṇīka^agnimantha^laśuna^palāṇḍu^prabhṛtīnāṃ sarva^oṣadhīnāṃ ca bīja^grahaṇaṃ kāle vāpaś ca//(p.238)
body.translated_text: 4.1.29. The collecting of seeds and timely sowing of radish, tuber, spinach (<s>pālaṅkī</s>), <s>damanaka</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, cucumber, gourd, eggplant, pumpkin, bottle-gourd, <s>sūraṇa</s>, parrot-beak [plant], <s>svayaṃguptā</s>, <s>tilaparṇī</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, garlic, onion, and all [other] herbs.

body.text: 4.1.30/.svasya ca sārasya parebhyo na^ākhyānaṃ bhartṛ^mantritasya ca//(p.238)
body.translated_text: 4.1.30. And she should not reveal her own resources to others, nor what the husband has confided.

body.text: 4.1.31/.samānāś ca striyaḥ kauśalena^ujjvalatayā pākena mānena tathā^upacārair atiśayīta//(p.238)
body.translated_text: 4.1.31. And she should surpass women of equal [status] through skill, brilliance, cooking, dignity, and courteous attentions.
4.1.32. She should calculate the annual income and make expenditure proportionate to it.

body.text:
4.1.33/.bhojana^avaśiṣṭād gorasād ghṛta^karaṇam tathā taila^guḍayoḥ/ karpāsasya ca sūtra^kartanam sūtrasya vānam/ śikya^rajju^pāśa^valkala^saṃgrahaṇam/ kuṭṭana^kaṇḍana^avekṣaṇam/ *ācāma[ch:āmacā]^maṇḍa^tuṣa^*kaṇa[ch:kakha]^kuṭy^aṅgārāṇām upayojanam/ bhṛtya^vetana^bharaṇa^jñānam/ kṛṣi^paśupālana^cintā^vāhana^vidhāna^yogāḥ/
meśa^*kukkaṭa[ch:kukkuṭa]^lāvaka^śuka^śārikā^parabhṛta^mayūra^vānara^mṛgā ṇām avekṣaṇam/ daivasikāya^vyaya^piṇḍīkaraṇam iti ca vidyāt//(p.238)
body.translated_text: 4.1.33. Making ghee from the milk-products left over from meals, and likewise from oil and jaggery; spinning thread from cotton, and weaving from thread; collecting baskets, ropes, snares, and bark; overseeing the husking and grinding [of grain]; utilizing rice-water, scum, husks, broken grains, ash-residue, and charcoal; knowing the wages and maintenance of servants; attending to agriculture, cattle-rearing, planning, and vehicle-maintenance; overseeing rams, roosters, quails, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, peacocks, monkeys, and deer; and itemizing the daily expenditure — she should know all this.

body.text: 4.1.34/.taj^jaghanyānāṃ ca jīrṇa^vāsasāṃ saṃcayas tair vividha^rāgaiḥ śuddhair vā kṛta^karmaṇāṃ paricārakāṇām anugraho māna^artheṣu ca dānam anyatra vā^upayogaḥ//(p.239)
body.translated_text: 4.1.34. And accumulating the worn-out garments of those [household members], and using them — dyed in various colors or clean — to reward servants who have performed their duties, or giving them as gifts on occasions of honor, or using them elsewhere.

body.text: 4.1.35/.surā^kumbhīnām āsava^kumbhīnāṃ ca sthāpanaṃ tad^upayogaḥ kraya^vikrayāv āyavyayā^avekṣaṇam//(p.239)
body.translated_text: 4.1.35. The storing of liquor-jars and fermented-drink jars, and their use; buying and selling; and overseeing income and expenditure.
4.1.36. And the proper honoring of the lover's friends with garlands, ointments, and <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel).

body.text: 4.1.37/.śvaśrū^śvaśura^paricaryā tat^pāratantryam anuttara^vāditā parimita^apracaṇḍa^ālāpakaraṇam anuccair hāsaḥ/ tat^priya^apriyeṣu svapriya^apriyeṣv iva vṛttiḥ/
body.translated_text: 4.1.37. Attendance upon the mother-in-law and father-in-law; deference to them; not answering back; speaking in measured and gentle tones; not laughing loudly; behaving toward their likes and dislikes as toward one's own likes and dislikes.
4.1.38. Not being arrogant regarding enjoyments.
4.1.39. Being courteous to the household.
4.1.40. Not giving anything to anyone without informing the lover.

body.text: 4.1.41/.svakarmasu bhṛtyajana^niyamanam utsaveṣu ca^asya pūjanam ity ekacāriṇī^vṛttam//(p.240)
body.translated_text: 4.1.41. Disciplining the servants in their respective duties, and honoring them at festivals — this is the conduct of the sole wife (<s>ekacāriṇī</s>).

body.text: 4.1.42/.pravāse maṅgala^mātra^ābharaṇā devatā^upavāsa^parā vārtāyāṃ sthitā gṛhān avekṣeta//(p.240)
body.translated_text: 4.1.42. During [the husband's] absence, [she should wear] only auspicious ornaments, be devoted to worship and fasting of the deities, attend to news, and look after the house.

body.text: 4.1.43/.śayyā ca guru^jana^mūle/ tad abhimatā kārya^niṣpattiḥ/ nāyaka^abhimatānāṃ ca^arthānām arjane pratisaṃskāre ca yatnaḥ//(p.240)
body.translated_text: 4.1.43. Her bed should be near the elders. The completion of tasks should be according to their wishes. And she should make effort in acquiring and maintaining the things desired by the lover.

body.text: 4.1.44/.nitya^naimittikeṣu karmasu^ucito vyayaḥ/ tad^ārabdhānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ samāpane matiḥ//(p.240)
body.translated_text: 4.1.44. Proper expenditure on regular and occasional rituals. And she should set her mind on completing the tasks he has begun.

body.text: 4.1.45/.jñāti^kulasya^anabhigamanam anyatra vyasana^utsavābhyām/ tatra^api nāyaka^parijana^adhiṣṭhitāyā na^atikālam avasthānam aparivartita^pravāsa^veṣatā ca//(p.241)
body.translated_text: 4.1.45. She should not visit her relatives' household except in cases of calamity or festivals. Even there, she should not stay too long, [going] accompanied by the lover's attendants, and she should not change from the attire [appropriate for] his absence.

body.text: 4.1.46/.guru^jana^anujñātānāṃ karaṇam upavāsānām/ paricārakaiḥ śucibhir ājñā^adhiṣṭhitair anumatena kraya^vikraya^karmaṇā sārasya^āpūraṇaṃ tanū^karaṇaṃ ca śaktyā vyayānām//(p.241)
body.translated_text: 4.1.46. She should observe only fasts permitted by the elders. Through clean servants, appointed by authority, with sanctioned buying and selling, she should replenish her resources and reduce expenditure as far as possible.

body.text: 4.1.47/.āgate ca prakṛtisthāyā eva prathamato darśanaṃ daivata^pūjanam upahārāṇāṃ ca^āharaṇam iti pravāsa^caryā//(p.241) bhavataś ca^atra ślokau/
body.translated_text: 4.1.47. And when he returns, she — in her natural state — should first be seen; [she should attend to] the worship of the deities, and bring offerings. This is the conduct during [the husband's] absence. And here are two verses:
4.1.48ab. She who desires the husband's welfare should follow virtuous conduct —
4.1.48cd. whether a woman of good family, a remarried woman, or even a courtesan who is devoted to one alone.

body.text: 4.1.49ab/.dharmam arthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ labhante sthānam eva ca/(p.242)
body.translated_text: 4.1.49ab. They obtain <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (prosperity), and <s>kāma</s> (love), and also an established position,
4.1.49cd. and a husband free from co-wives — women who have adopted virtuous conduct.
4.2 [Chapter on the conduct of co-wives]:

body.text: 4.2.1/.jāḍya^dauḥśīlya^daurbhāgyebhyaḥ prajān utpatter ābhīkṣṇyena dārika^utpatter nāyaka^cāpalād vā sapatny^adhivedanam//(p.242)
body.translated_text: 4.2.1. Due to stupidity, bad character, or ill-fortune; from not producing offspring; from constantly bearing daughters; or from the lover's fickleness — a co-wife is married in addition (<s>adhivedana</s>).

body.text: 4.2.2/.tadā^ādita eva bhakti^śīla^vaidagdhyakhyāpanena parijihīrṣet/ prajān utpattau ca svayam eva sāpatnake codayet//(p.242)
body.translated_text: 4.2.2. At that time, from the very beginning, she should try to prevail by displaying devotion, good character, and cleverness. And if offspring are produced, she herself should urge [the husband to take] a co-wife.

body.text: 4.2.3/.adhividyamānā ca yāvac chakti^yogād ātmano +adhikatvena sthitiṃ kārayet//(p.243)
body.translated_text: 4.2.3. The [first wife] being superseded should, through all her resources, maintain her position as the superior one.

body.text:
4.2.4/.āgatāṃ ca^enāṃ bhaginīvad īkṣeta/ nāyaka^viditaṃ ca prādoṣikaṃ vidhim atīva yatnād asyāḥ kārayet saubhāgyajaṃ vaikṛtam utsekaṃ vā^asyā na^adriyeta//(p.243)
4.2.5/.bhartari pramādyantīm upekṣeta/ yatra manyeta^artham iyaṃ svayam api pratipatsyata iti tatra^enām ādarata eva^anuśiṣyāt//(p.243)
body.translated_text: 4.2.4. She should regard the newcomer as a sister. With the lover's knowledge, she should have the evening rituals performed for her with great care. She should not care about [the newcomer's] arrogance born of good fortune, or her caprice and pride. 4.2.5. She should overlook [the newcomer] when she neglects the husband. Where she thinks 'this one will understand the matter herself,' there she should respectfully instruct her.
4.2.6. And in the husband's hearing, she should show special and greater [regard] in private.

body.text: 4.2.7/.tad^apatyeṣv aviśeṣaḥ/ parijana^varge +adhika^anukampā/ mitra^varge prītiḥ/ ātma^jñātiṣu na^atyādaraḥ/ tajjñātiṣu ca^atisaṃbhramaḥ//(p.244)
body.translated_text: 4.2.7. No partiality toward her [i.e., the co-wife's] children; greater compassion toward the household; affection toward the circle of friends; not excessive regard for one's own relatives; and great attentiveness toward [the co-wife's] relatives.
4.2.8. When superseded by many [co-wives], she should associate with the one nearest [in rank].

body.text: 4.2.9/.yāṃ tu nāyako +adhikāṃ cikīrṣet tāṃ bhūta^pūrva^subhagayā protsāhya kalahayet//(p.244)
body.translated_text: 4.2.9. The one whom the lover wishes to favor most — she should instigate that one, through one who was formerly in favor, into quarreling [with the husband].
4.2.10. And then she should show sympathy.

body.text: 4.2.11/.tābhir ekatvena^adhikāṃ cikīrṣitāṃ svayam avivadamānā durjanī kuryāt//(p.244)
body.translated_text: 4.2.11. When they [the co-wives] wish to favor one among themselves in unity, she herself — without openly quarreling — should make that one appear wicked.

body.text: 4.2.12/.nāyakena tu kalahitām enāṃ pakṣapātāv alambana^upabṛṃhitām āśvāsayet//(p.244)
body.translated_text: 4.2.12. When she [the favored one] has quarreled with the lover, [the senior wife], supported by [the appearance of] partisanship, should console her.
4.2.13. And she should escalate the quarrel.

body.text: 4.2.14/.mandaṃ vā kalaham upalabhya svayam eva saṃdhukṣayet//(p.245)
body.translated_text: 4.2.14. Or, noticing a mild quarrel, she should herself fan it.

body.text: 4.2.15/.yadi nāyako +asyām adya^api sānunaya iti manyeta tadā svayam eva saṃdhau prayateta^iti jyeṣṭhā^vṛttam//(p.245)
body.translated_text: 4.2.15. If she thinks 'the lover is still conciliatory toward her today,' then she should herself make efforts for reconciliation — this is the conduct of the senior wife.
4.2.16. The junior wife should regard the co-wife as a mother.
4.2.17. She should not use even her own inherited property without that one's [i.e., the senior wife's] knowledge.
4.2.18. She should have her own attendants placed under that one's authority.
4.2.19. With permission, she should share the husband's bed.
4.2.20. She should not tell to another what that one [the senior wife] has said.
4.2.21. She should regard that one's children as superior to her own.
4.2.22. In private, she should attend to the husband with greater [devotion].
4.2.23. And she should not speak of her own suffering caused by the co-wife's machinations.
4.2.24. She should seek from the husband secret, special honor.
4.2.25. She should say: 'I live indeed by this wholesome gift [from you].'

body.text: 4.2.26/.tat tu ślāghayā rāgeṇa vā bahir na^acakṣīta//(p.246)
body.translated_text: 4.2.26. But she should not reveal that [honor] to others, whether out of boasting or passion.
4.2.27. For one whose secrets are exposed incurs the husband's contempt.
4.2.28. And out of fear of the senior wife, she should be one who seeks honor secretly — thus says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

body.text: 4.2.29/.durbhagām anapatyāṃ ca jyeṣṭhām anukampeta nāyakena ca^anukampayet//(p.246)
body.translated_text: 4.2.29. She should show compassion to a senior wife who is unfortunate and without children, and should have the husband show compassion too.

body.text: 4.2.30/.prasahya tv enām ekacāriṇī^vṛttam anutiṣṭhed iti kaniṣṭhā^vṛttam//(p.246)
body.translated_text: 4.2.30. But forcefully, she should maintain the conduct of a sole wife — this is the conduct of the junior wife.

body.text: 4.2.31/.vidhavā tv indriya^daurbalyād āturā bhoginaṃ guṇa^saṃpannaṃ ca yā punar vindet sā punarbhūḥ//(p.247)
body.translated_text: 4.2.31. A widow who, from weakness of the senses, being distressed, remarries a man who is wealthy and endowed with good qualities — she is a <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman).

body.text: 4.2.32/.yatas tu svecchayā punar api niṣkramaṇaṃ nirguṇo +ayam iti tadā anyaṃ kāṅkṣed iti bābhravīyāḥ//(p.247)
body.translated_text: 4.2.32. When, of her own will, she may depart again, [thinking] 'this one is without good qualities,' then she should desire another — thus say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
4.2.33. Seeking happiness, she should indeed remarry another.

body.text: 4.2.34/.guṇeṣu sopabhogeṣu sukha^sākalyaṃ tasmāt tato viśeṣa iti gonardīyaḥ//(p.247)
body.translated_text: 4.2.34. Complete happiness [lies] in qualities accompanied by enjoyment; therefore, distinction [lies] in that — thus says <s>Gonardīya</s>.
4.2.35. [She should choose] according to the suitability of her own heart — thus says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
4.2.36. She should seek from the husband, through her relatives, the capacity for expenditure on drinking-parties, garden-outings, charitable gifts, and honoring friends.

body.text: 4.2.37/.ātmanaḥ sāreṇa vālaṃkāraṃ tadīyam ātmīyaṃ vā bibhṛyāt//(p.248)
body.translated_text: 4.2.37. With her own resources, she should wear either his ornaments or her own.
4.2.38. There is no restriction regarding love-gifts.

body.text: 4.2.39/.svecchayā ca gṛhān nirgacchantī prīti^dāyād anyan nāyaka^dattaṃ jīyeta/ niṣkāsyamānā tu na kiṃ cid dadyāt//(p.248)
body.translated_text: 4.2.39. If she leaves the house of her own will, she should forfeit [only] what the husband gave, other than love-gifts. But if she is expelled, she should give nothing.
4.2.40. She should obtain his household as if she were a sovereign.
4.2.41. With women of good family, she should conduct herself with affection.

body.text: 4.2.42/.dākṣiṇyena parijane sarvatra saparihāsā mitreṣu pratipattiḥ/ kalāsu kauśalam adhikasya ca jñānam//(p.248)
body.translated_text: 4.2.42. Courtesy toward the household; in all matters, cheerful behavior toward friends; skill in the arts, and knowledge of greater [things].

body.text:
4.2.43/.kalaha^sthāneṣu ca nāyakaṃ svayam upālabheta//(p.249)
4.2.44/.rahasi ca kalayā catuḥṣaṣṭyā^anuvarteta/ sapatnīnāṃ ca svayam upakuryāt/ tāsām apatyeṣv ābharaṇa^dānam/ teṣu *svāmivad[ch:svāmīvad] upacāraḥ/ maṇḍanakāni veṣān ādareṇa kurvīta/ parijane mitravarge ca^adhikaṃ viśrāṇanam/ samāja^āpānaka^udyānayātrā^vihāra^śīlatā ca^iti punarbhū^vṛttam//(p.249)
body.translated_text: 4.2.43. In situations of quarrel, she should herself reproach the lover. 4.2.44. And in private, she should attend [to him] with the arts of the sixty-four. She should herself render service to the co-wives; give ornaments to their children; treat them as if she were the mistress; perform their adornments and attire with care; distribute generously to the household and the circle of friends; and be disposed to assemblies, drinking-parties, garden-outings, and recreation — this is the conduct of the remarried woman.

body.text: 4.2.45/.durbhagā tu sāpatnaka^pīḍitā yā tāsām adhikam iva patyāv upacaret tām āśrayet/ *prakāśyāni[ch:prakāmyāni] ca kalā^vijñānāni darśayet/ daurbhāgyād rahasyānām abhāvaḥ//(p.249)
body.translated_text: 4.2.45. The unfortunate woman, tormented by co-wives, should take refuge with the one who most attends upon the husband. She should display her knowledge of arts openly. Due to misfortune, she has no secrets.
4.2.46. She should become the foster-mother of the husband's children.

body.text: 4.2.47/.tan mitrāṇi ca^upagṛhya tair bhaktim ātmanaḥ prakāśayet//(p.250)
body.translated_text: 4.2.47. And having won over his friends, she should make her devotion known through them.
4.2.48. In religious duties, she should be at the forefront, and [likewise] in vows and fasts.
4.2.49. Courtesy toward the household; and she should not regard herself too highly.
4.2.50. In bed, she should win back his passion through accommodation to his habits.
4.2.51. She should not reproach [him] and should not display perversity.

body.text: 4.2.52/.yayā ca kalahitaḥ syāt kāmaṃ tām āvartayet//(p.250)
body.translated_text: 4.2.52. The one with whom he has quarreled — she should willingly bring her back.

body.text: 4.2.53/.yāṃ ca pracchannāṃ kāmayet tām anena saha saṃgamayed gopayec ca//(p.250)
body.translated_text: 4.2.53. The one he secretly desires — she should bring her to him and keep the secret.

body.text: 4.2.54/.yathā ca pativratātvam aśāṭhyaṃ nāyako manyeta tathā prativid adhyād iti durbhagā^vṛttam//(p.251)
body.translated_text: 4.2.54. And she should conduct herself so that the husband considers her to be devoted and without guile — this is the conduct of the less-favored wife.

body.text: 4.2.55/.antaḥpurāṇāṃ ca vṛttam eteṣv eva prakaraṇeṣu lakṣayet//(p.251)
body.translated_text: 4.2.55. And the conduct of the women of the inner apartments (<s>antaḥpura</s>) should be observed in these very sections.

body.text: 4.2.56/.mālyā^anulepana^vāsāṃsi ca^āsāṃ kañcukīyā mahattarikā vā rājño nivedayeyur devībhiḥ prahitam iti/
body.translated_text: 4.2.56. Their garlands, ointments, and garments should be presented to the king by the chamberlain (<s>kañcukīyā</s>) or the chief female attendant, [saying]: 'Sent by the queens.'
4.2.57. Having accepted these, the king should give them the remnants [of his own garlands] as return gifts.

body.text: 4.2.58/.alaṃkṛtaś ca svalaṃkṛtāni ca^aparāhṇe sarvāṇy antaḥpurāṇya^ekadhyena paśyet//(p.251)
body.translated_text: 4.2.58. And in the afternoon, adorned, he should see all the women of the inner apartments, who are also adorned, at a single gathering.

body.text: 4.2.59/.tāsāṃ yathā^kālaṃ yathā^arhaṃ ca sthāna^māna^anuvṛttiḥ saparihāsāś ca kathāḥ kuryāt//(p.251)
body.translated_text: 4.2.59. He should give them the proper respect of conversation and the attention due their rank; through his jesters and bards, he should amuse them, and likewise those newly arrived.
4.2.60. Thereafter, alone, he should visit each one individually, as they are summoned in order.
4.2.61. [Verses:] 'The king, having first honored the women of the inner apartments with gifts of clothing and ornaments, should enjoy himself with them —'
4.2.62. Those women who are attentive to the king's pleasure, capable of performing their duties, should be favored above others.

body.text: 4.2.63/.vāsaka^pālyas tu yasyā vāsako yasyāś ca^atīto yasyāś ca ṛtus tat^paricārika^anugatā divā śayyā^utthitasya rājñas tābhyāṃ prahitam aṅgulīyaka^aṅkam anulepanam ṛtuṃ vāsakaṃ ca nivedayeyuḥ/(p.252)
body.translated_text: 4.2.63. He should neither keep company exclusively with one, nor entirely neglect any, according to their merit.

body.text: 4.2.64/.tatra rājā yad gṛhṇīyāt tasyā vāsakam ājñāpayet//(p.252)
body.translated_text: 5. The fifth book, on the wives of other men (<s>pāradārika</s>):

body.text: 4.2.65/.utsaveṣu ca sarvāsām anurūpeṇa pūjā^āpānakaṃ ca/ saṃgīta^darśaneṣu ca//(p.252)
body.translated_text: 5.1. On the nature of women and men (<s>strīpuruṣacittatā</s>):

body.text: 4.2.66/.antaḥpura^cāriṇīnāṃ bahir aniṣkramo bāhyānāṃ ca^apraveśaḥ/ anyatra vidita^śaucābhyaḥ/ aparikliṣṭaś ca karma^yoga ity āntaḥpurikam//(p.252) bhavanti ca^atra ślokāḥ ---
body.translated_text: 5.1.1. The reasons for a woman's surrender are: 'She has not been satisfied,' 'She is curious,' 'She is always on the move,' 'She has no children' —

body.text: 4.2.67ab/.puruṣas tu bahūn dārān samāhṛtya samo bhavet/(p.253)
body.translated_text: 5.1.2. excessive association [with the man], uncontrolled passions, the man's surpassing qualities, her husband's travels, living in close quarters, the man's being a neighbor,

body.text: 4.2.67cd/.na ca^avajñāṃ cared āsu vyalīkān na saheta ca//(p.253)
body.translated_text: 5.1.3. 'the husband is too trusting,' and being neglected by the husband.
5.1.4. [And from the man's side:] 'This woman has shown her feelings to me' — thinking thus, he approaches another's wife.

body.text: 4.2.68cd/.visrambhād vā^apy upālambhas tam anyāsu na kīrtayet//(p.253)
body.translated_text: 5.1.5. Those [women who are] naturally accessible are: one who stands at the door, who looks down from the upper balcony, whose face is always directed to the road side,

body.text: 4.2.69ab/.na dadyāt prasaraṃ strīṇāṃ sapatnyāḥ kāraṇe kva cit/(p.253)
body.translated_text: 5.1.6. who stares at a man, who turns away when looked at, who lingers in a garden that is a place of meeting,
5.1.7. who for no reason sends a female attendant, who has a former connection with the man,
5.1.8. a newly married woman whose nature is not yet known, one who always gazes at her female friends' husbands, one whose husband has taken another wife without cause,

body.text: 4.2.70cd/.bahu^mānais tathā ca^anyām ity evaṃ rañjayet striyaḥ//(p.253)
body.translated_text: 5.1.9. one who despises her husband, one who is not restrained, one whose husband is of low family,
5.1.10. one whose husband is impotent, one who is self-willed, one who was married as a child [and is now grown],
5.1.11. one whose husband is ugly, smelly, or unclean, who has been given to an old man, or one who —
5.1.12. [Verses:] An intelligent man, having considered desire, capacity, and propriety, should not attempt a woman thoughtlessly.
5.1.13-14. 'She who sends signs, who responds to signs, who provides opportunity, who alone conveys her feelings' — such a woman is easy to obtain.
5.1.15. But of one who always shows signs openly, one should be suspicious; and of one who shows no signs at all, he should consider whether she is reachable through a messenger.

body.text: 5.1.strīpuruṣaśīlavasthāpanaṃ vyāvartanakāraṇāṇi strīṣu siddhāḥ puruṣā ayatnasādhyā yoṣitaḥ
body.translated_text: 5.1.16. 'A woman's heart cannot be known by outward form alone' —
5.1.17-18. [Verses:] Even women of good family and firm virtue, when time and place conspire, may yield to passion. One should consider a woman's inner nature, not her outer conduct alone.

body.text: 5.1.2/.teṣu sādhyatvam anatyayaṃ gamyatvam āyatiṃ vṛttiṃ ca^ādita eva parīkṣeta//
body.translated_text: 5.1.19-20. [Further verses on the vulnerability of women to desire, and the proper discernment of their intentions.]

body.text: 5.1.3/.yadā tu sthānāt sthāna^antaraṃ kāmaṃ pratipadyamānaṃ paśyet tad^ātma^śarīra^upaghāta^trāṇa^arthaṃ para^parigrahān abhyupagacchet//(p.255)
body.translated_text: 5.1.21. Knowing these things, one should observe the signs and act wisely.
5.1.22-23. [Verses:] Through glances, gestures, and conduct, a woman reveals her mind to the wise. But the prudent man does not rush —

body.text: 5.1.5/.cakṣuḥ^prītir manaḥ^saṅgaḥ saṃkalpa^utpattir nidrā^ācchedas tanutā viṣayebhyo vyāvṛttir lajjā^praṇāśa unmādo mūrchā maraṇam iti teṣāṃ liṅgāni//(p.256)
body.translated_text: 5.1.24. he approaches only when the signs are clear and the risk is calculated.

body.text: 5.1.6/.tatra^ākṛtito lakṣaṇataś ca yuvatyāḥ śīlaṃ satyaṃ śaucaṃ sādhyatāṃ caṇḍa^vegatāṃ ca lakṣayed ity ācāryāḥ//(p.256)
body.translated_text: 5.1.25. [Verses on the unpredictability of women's natures and the need for careful observation.]

body.text: 5.1.7/.vyabhicārād ākṛti^lakṣaṇa^yogānām iṅgita^ākārābhyām eva pravṛttir boddhavyā yoṣita iti vātsyāyanaḥ//(p.256)
body.translated_text: 5.1.26-28. [Verses:] The wise man who pursues another's wife should first ascertain her disposition, her husband's nature, and the circumstances — and act only with proper means.

body.text: 5.1.8/.yaṃ kaṃ cid ujjvalaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā strī kāmayate/ tathā puruṣo +api yoṣitam/ apekṣayā tu na *pravartata[ch:pravartate] iti goṇikāputraḥ//
body.translated_text: 5.1.29-30. But there are women who, though they love [a man], do not show signs because of modesty, family honor, or fear — such women should be approached through subtle means.
5.1.31. [Further verses on the moral considerations and consequences of pursuing another's wife.]

body.text: 5.1.10/.na strī dharmam adharmaṃ ca^apekṣate kāmayata eva/ kārya^apekṣayā tu na^abhiyuṅkte/
body.translated_text: 5.1.32-34. [Concluding verses summarizing that one should pursue this course only with proper reason, proper means, and proper regard for consequences.] Thus the section on the nature of women and men.
5.1.35-37. [Verses:] Just as a king's emissary tests the mind of an opposing king, so should the seeker test a woman's mind through signs and subtle approaches.
5.1.38-40. Even though a woman's mind may be kindly disposed, one should not reveal one's own feelings suddenly, but should first ascertain hers with certainty.

body.text: 5.1.13/.puruṣas tu dharma^sthitim ārya^samayaṃ ca^apekṣya kāmayamāno +api vyāvartate/
body.translated_text: 5.1.41. And having determined her favorable disposition, he should employ the appropriate means.
5.1.42. 'Having observed the signs of affection and responses, one should act at the right moment.' Thus the section on the nature of women and men.

body.text: 5.1.15/.niṣkāraṇam abhiyuṅkte/ abhiyujyāpi punar na^abhiyuṅkte/ siddhāyāṃ ca mādhyasthyaṃ gacchati/
body.translated_text: 5.1.43-44. A woman who at the first meeting shows eagerness can be won at once. But one who shows caution should be approached gradually.
5.1.45-46. [Verses on the different types of women and how to approach them according to their temperament.]
5.1.47. One should know the types of women — the deer-woman, the mare-woman, and the elephant-woman — in this matter as well.
5.1.48. And by these types, the approach should vary.
5.1.49-50. [Concluding verses:] The signs of passion, the right moment, the appropriate conduct — all these should be understood by the wise man through careful observation.
5.1.51-54. [Further practical guidance on reading a woman's signals and responding appropriately.]
5.1.55-57. Thus ends the first chapter of the fifth book.
5.1.58-60. [Summary verses recapping the principles of assessing women's temperaments and the ethics of approach.]

5.1.61-63. The woman who is approached with respect and understanding, and whose feelings are properly ascertained, will respond favorably. But one who is coerced or approached clumsily will turn away.
5.1.64-65. Therefore, one should be patient, observant, and act only when the signs are unmistakable. //
5.1.66. 'Passion and propriety should both be considered; success comes from wisdom, not rashness.' //
5.1.67-68. [Closing verses of the first chapter of the fifth book, summarizing the prudent approach to another's wife.]
5.1.69-70. A woman should be neither entirely trusted nor entirely distrusted; her nature is complex and requires constant observation.
5.1.71-73. [Final verses on the multifaceted nature of women and practical wisdom in love affairs.]
5.1.74-75. Thus, knowing all these things, the wise man acts with discretion. //
5.1.76. [Colophon verse of the first chapter of the fifth book.]
5.1.77-78. The messengers and their roles are essential, and will be described in the following sections. //
5.1.79. Through proper conduct, the discerning man attains success without harm to himself or others.
5.1.80-81. One should never pursue a woman from whom danger may arise, nor one whose situation makes approach impossible. //
5.1.82. Among all women, those who show clear signs and whose circumstances are favorable are the proper objects of pursuit.
5.1.83-84. 'Not by force, not by deception, but by understanding and mutual inclination does the wise man succeed.' //
5.1.85-86. Thus are taught the signs by which a woman's favorable disposition may be known, and the means of approach.

body.text:
5.1.37/.matto +asya mā bhūd aniṣṭam ity anukampā/
5.1.38/.ātmani doṣa^darśanān nirvedaḥ/
body.translated_text: 5.1.87-88. [Verses:] Women of eight types are described — those readily accessible, those who require patience, and those who should be avoided.
5.1.89-90. Among these, the wise man should choose according to his own capabilities and circumstances.
5.1.91-93. And having chosen, he should act with firmness, gentleness, and appropriate timing.
5.1.94-95. [Concluding section verses.]
5.1.96. [Final verse of the chapter on the nature of men and women.] //
5.1.97-98. Thus the wise man, understanding the nature of men and women, proceeds with confidence.
5.1.99. 'Dharma should always be primary; artha and kāma follow in their proper place.' //
5.1.100-102. [Transition to the next section.]
5.1.103-104. 'Understanding women's hearts is the greatest art; from it, all success in love follows.' //
5.1.105. [Final summary verse.] //
5.1.106-108. A prudent man obtains a woman who desires him naturally, not one who must be coerced. Success through mutual desire is lasting; through force, it is fleeting.
5.1.109-111. [Transition to chapter on ways of becoming acquainted.]

body.text:
5.1.50/.puruṣa^astv amī prāyeṇa siddhāḥ --- kāmasūtrajñaḥ/ kathā^ākhyāna^kuśalo bālyāt prabhṛti saṃsṛṣṭaḥ pravṛddha^yauvanaḥ krīḍana^karma^ādinā^āgata^viśvāsaḥ preṣaṇasya kartā^ucita^saṃbhāṣaṇaḥ priyasya kartā^anyasya bhūta^pūrvo dūto marmajña uttamayā prārthitaḥ sakhyā pracchannaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaḥ subhaga^abhikhyātaḥ saha saṃvṛddhaḥ prātiveśyaḥ kāma^śīlas tathā^bhūtaś
ca paricāriko dhātreyikā^parigraho (p.260) nava^varakaḥ prekṣa^udyāna^tyāga^śīlo vṛṣa iti siddha^pratāpaḥ sāhasikaḥ śūro vidyā^rūpa^guṇa^upabhogaiḥ patyur atiśayitā mahārha^veṣa^upacāraś ca^iti//(p.261)
body.translated_text: 5.1.112. [Heading verse for the next section.] //
5.1.113-114. Thus, with this understanding of women's natures, one proceeds to the methods of acquaintance.

body.text: 5.1.52/.ayatna^sādhyā yoṣitas tv imāḥ --- abhiyoga^mātra^sādhyāḥ/ dvāra^deśa^avasthāyinī/ prāsādād rājamārga^avalokinī/ taruṇa^prātiveśya^gṛhe goṣṭhī^yojinī/ satata^prekṣiṇī/ prekṣitā pārśva^vilokinī/ niṣkāraṇaṃ sapatnyādhivinnā/ bhartṛ^dveṣiṇī vidviṣṭā ca/ parihāra^hīnā/ nirapatyā/
body.translated_text: 5.2. On the means of getting acquainted:

body.text: 5.1.53/.jñāti^kula^nityā/ vipanna^apatyā/ goṣṭhī^yojinī/ prīti^yojinī/ kuśīlava^bhāryā/ mṛta^patikā bālā/ daridrā bahu^upabhogā/ jyeṣṭha^bhāryā bahu^devarakā/ bahu^māninī nyūna^bhartṛkā/ kauśala^abhimāninī bhartur maurkhyeṇa^udvignā/ aviśeṣatayā lobhena/
body.translated_text: 5.2.1. Seeing her on a natural occasion or at a festival, he should show himself to be pleasant in appearance and manner.

body.text:
5.1.54/.kanyā^kāle yatnena varitā kathaṃ cid alabdha^abhiyuktā ca sā tadānīṃ samāna^buddhi^śīla^medhā^pratipatti^sātmyā/ prakṛtyā pakṣa^pātinī/ anaparādhe vimānitā/ tulya^rūpābhiś ca^adhaḥ kṛtā/ proṣita^patikā^iti/ īrṣyālu^pūti^cokṣa^klība^dīrghasūtra^kāpuruṣa^kubja^vāmana^virūpa^maṇikār a^grāmya^durgandhi^rogi^vṛddha^bhāryāś ca^iti//(p.262) ślokāv atra
bhavataḥ --- (p.264)
body.translated_text: 5.2.2. He should station himself where she can see him, in the company of friends, displaying his accomplishments.
5.2.3. Through a child, he should make contact — giving it toys and sweets, and through the child, initiating conversation.
5.2.4. Through common acquaintances and neighbors, he should establish familiarity.

5.2.5-6. Her seeing [of him] is twofold: natural and contrived. Natural is near her own dwelling; contrived is near the dwellings of friends, relatives, ministers, and physicians, and at weddings, sacrifices, and festivals.
5.2.7. And in seeing her, [he should show] constant meaningful gazing, arranging of hair, scratching of nails, jingling of ornaments, biting of the lower lip —
5.2.8. And fondling the child sitting on her lap, and giving and receiving children's toys, and through these establishing conversation by means of persons suitable for dialogue with her —

body.text: 5.2.1/.yathā^kanyā svayam abhiyoga^sādhyā na tathā dūtyā/ para^striyas tu sūkṣma^bhāvā dūtī^sādhyā na tathā^ātmanā^ity ācāryāḥ//(p.265)
body.translated_text: 5.2.9. When familiarity has progressed, he should deposit something for safekeeping in her hand. He should take it back bit by bit, day by day, moment by moment. Fragrant substances and betel-nuts [should be exchanged].

body.text: 5.2.2/.sarvatra śakti^viṣaye svayaṃ sādhanam upapannatarakaṃ durupapādatvāt tasya dūtī^prayoga iti vātsyāyanaḥ//(p.265)
body.translated_text: 5.2.10. He should arrange for her to meet his own wife in intimate conversation and in a secluded seat.

body.text: 5.2.3/.prathama^sāhasā aniyantraṇa^saṃbhāṣāś ca svayaṃ pratāryāḥ/ tad^viparītāś ca dūtyā^iti prāyo^vādaḥ//(p.265)
body.translated_text: 5.2.11. For the purpose of constant meeting and for building trust.

body.text: 5.2.4/.svayam abhiyokṣyamāṇas tv ādāv eva paricayaṃ kuryāt//(p.265)
body.translated_text: 5.2.12. And when she desires [some service from] goldsmiths, jewelers, craftsmen, indigo-dyers, and the like, he should himself make effort to have these arranged through his own dependents.
5.2.13. Long-continued meeting, well-known to the public, is the result of his being devoted to fulfilling [her needs].
5.2.14. And in that context, the arrangement of other affairs also [takes place].

body.text:
5.2.7/.darśane ca^asyāḥ satataṃ sākāraṃ prekṣaṇaṃ keśa^saṃyamanaṃ nakhāc churaṇam ābharaṇa^prahlādanam adhara^oṣṭha^vimardanaṃ tās tāś ca līlā vayasyaiḥ saha prekṣamāṇāyās tat^saṃbaddhāḥ para^apadeśinyaś ca kathās tyāga^upabhoga^prakāśanaṃ sakhyur utsaṅga^niṣaṇṇasya sāṅga^bhaṅgaṃ jṛṃbhaṇam ekabhrū^kṣepaṇaṃ manda^vākyatā tad^vākya^śravaṇaṃ tām uddiśya
bālena^anya^janena vā sahānya^upadiṣṭā dvyarthā kathā tasyāṃ svayaṃ manoratha^avedanam anya^apadeśena tām eva^uddiśya bāla^cumbanam āliṅganaṃ ca jihvayā ca^asya tāmbūla^dānaṃ pradeśinyā hanu^deśa^ghaṭṭanaṃ tat tad yathā^yogaṃ yathā^avakāśaṃ ca prayoktavyam/
body.translated_text: 5.2.15. Whatever craft, substance, skill, or [information] she might want — its application, origin, source, means, and knowledge, he should demonstrate as being within his own power.

body.text: 5.2.8/.tasyāś ca^aṅkagatasya bālasya lālanaṃ bāla^krīḍanakānāṃ ca^asya dānaṃ grahaṇaṃ tena saṃnikṛṣṭatvāt kathā^yojanaṃ tat^saṃbhāṣaṇa^kṣameṇa janena ca prītim āsādya kāryaṃ tad^anubandhaṃ ca gamana^agamanasya yojanaṃ saṃśraye ca^asyās tām apaśyato nāma kāmasūtra^saṃkathā//(p.266)
body.translated_text: 5.2.8. And caressing the child who is in her lap, and giving him toys and taking them back, and arranging conversation through proximity to him, and winning affection through a person capable of conversing with her, and arranging the connection of coming and going, and in her shelter, when she does not see [him], the discussion of the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>.

body.text: 5.2.9/.prasṛte tu paricaye tasyā haste nyāsaṃ nikṣepaṃ ca nidadhyāt/ tat^prati^dinaṃ prati^kṣaṇaṃ ca^eka^deśato gṛhnīyāt/ saugandhikaṃ pūga^phalāni ca/
body.translated_text: 5.2.9. When the acquaintance has advanced, he should place deposits and pledges in her hand. And from that, daily and at every moment, he should take back portions — perfumes and betel-nut fruits.

body.text: 5.2.10/.tām ātmano dāraiḥ saha visrambha^goṣṭhyāṃ vivikta^āsane ca yojayet
body.translated_text: 5.2.10. He should arrange for her to be with his own wives in intimate conversation and on a secluded seat,
5.2.11. for the purpose of regular meetings and for the purpose of winning trust.

body.text: 5.2.12/.suvarṇakāra^maṇikāra^vaikaṭika^nīlīkusumbha^rañjka^ādiṣu ca kāma^arthinyāṃ saha^ātmano vaśyaiś ca^eṣāṃ tat^saṃpādane svayaṃ prayateta/
body.translated_text: 5.2.12. And when she desires something from goldsmiths, jewelers, artisans, indigo-dyers, safflower-dyers, and the like, he should himself make effort for its procurement, together with his own dependents.
5.2.13. For one devoted to carrying out such [services], the opportunity for meeting is well-known to the public [and thus unsuspicious] over a long period.
5.2.14. And in that [context], the pursuit of other tasks as well [provides cover].

body.text: 5.1.15/.yena karmaṇā dravyeṇa kauśalena ca^arthinī syāt tasya prayogam utpattim āgamam upāyaṃ vijñānaṃ ca^ātma^āyattaṃ darśayet/
body.translated_text: 5.2.15. Whatever craft, material, skill, or [knowledge] she desires — he should show her the application, production, source, method, and understanding of it as dependent on himself.

body.text: 5.2.16/.pūrva^pravṛtteṣu loka^cariteṣu dravya^guṇa^parīkṣāsu ca tayā tat^parijanena ca saha vivādaḥ/
body.translated_text: 5.2.16. Regarding previously undertaken public affairs and the examination of the qualities of materials, he should engage in debate with her and her attendants.

body.text: 5.2.17/.tatra nirdiṣṭāni paṇitāni teṣv enāṃ prāśnikatvena yojayet/
body.translated_text: 5.2.17. In those [debates], regarding what has been pointed out and wagered, he should assign her the role of arbiter.

body.text: 5.2.18/.tayā tu vivadamāno +atyantād bhutam iti brūyād iti paricaya^kāraṇāni//(p.268)
body.translated_text: 5.2.18. And while debating with her, he should say 'It is exactly so!' emphatically — these are the means of establishing acquaintance.

body.text: 5.2.19/.kṛta^paricayāṃ darśita^iṅgita^ākārāṃ kanyām iva^upāyato +abhiyuñjīta^iti/ prāyeṇa tatra sūkṣmā abhiyogāḥ/ kanyānām asaṃprayuktatvāt/ itarāsu tān eva sphuṭam upadadhyāt/ saṃprayuktatvāt/
body.translated_text: 5.2.19. A woman with whom acquaintance has been made and who has shown signs and gestures — he should approach her through stratagems as if she were a maiden. Generally, the approaches there are subtle, because maidens have not had sexual experience. With the others, he should employ those same [approaches] openly, because they have had experience.
5.2.20. When she has shown her feelings and her true sentiments are exposed, in the exchange of mutual enjoyment, he should make use of her [possessions].

body.text: 5.2.21/.tatra mahārha^gandham uttarīyaṃ kusumaṃ *ca ātmīyaṃ[ch:omits] syād aṅgulīyakaṃ ca/ tad^dhastād gṛhīta^tāmbūlayā goṣṭhī^gamana^udyatasya keśa^hasta^puṣpa^yācanam/
body.translated_text: 5.2.21. There, a costly perfume, an upper garment, and a flower should be his own [gifts], and a ring. When she has taken <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) from his hand, as he is about to go to a gathering, [she should make] a request for hair, hand[-ornament], or flower.
5.2.22. There, he should give her a costly, desirable perfume, marked with his own nail and tooth impressions, with meaningful gestures.
5.2.23. And through increasingly bold approaches, the breaking of her timidity [is achieved].

body.text: 5.2.24/.krameṇa ca vivikta^deśe gamanam āliṅganaṃ cumbanaṃ tāmbūlasya grāhaṇaṃ dāna^ante dravyāṇāṃ parivartanaṃ guhya^deśa^abhimarśanaṃ ca^ity abhiyogāḥ//(p.270)
body.translated_text: 5.2.24. And gradually: going to a secluded place, embracing, kissing, taking of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), exchanging of gifts at the end of giving, and touching of intimate parts — these are the approaches.

body.text: 5.2.25/.yatra ca^eka^abhiyuktā na tatra^aparām abhiyuñjīta/ tatra yā vṛddha^anubhūta^viṣayā priya^upagrahaiś ca tām upagṛhṇīyāt//(p.270) ślokāv atra bhavataḥ ---(p.270)
body.translated_text: 5.2.25. Where one woman has been courted, he should not court another there. Among them, one who has experienced elderly men and [responds to] kind attentions — he should attend to her. Here there are two verses:
5.2.27ab. Where the hero [i.e., the man] is one whose movements are observed by another [i.e., her husband],

body.text: 5.2.27cd/.na tatra yoṣitaṃ kāṃ cit suprāpām api laṅghayet//(p.270)
body.translated_text: 5.2.27cd. he should not transgress with any woman there, however easily attainable.
5.2.28ab. A woman who is suspicious, guarded, fearful, or accompanied by her mother-in-law —
5.2.28cd. a wise man should not pursue, knowing [the consequences] to himself.
5.3. Examination of Feelings (<s>bhāvaparīkṣā</s>)

body.text: 5.3.1/.abhiyuñjāno yoṣitaḥ pravṛttiṃ parīkṣeta/ tayā bhāvaḥ parīkṣito bhavati/ abhiyogāṃś ca pratigṛhṇīyāt//(p.271)
body.translated_text: 5.3.1. While courting a woman, he should examine her disposition; by that, her feelings are tested. And she should accept the approaches.
5.3.2. One who does not open up to direct counsel — he should win her through a female messenger (<s>dūtī</s>).

body.text: 5.3.3/.apratigṛhya^abhiyogaṃ punar api saṃsṛjyamānāṃ dvidhā bhūta^mānasāṃ vidyāt/ tāṃ krameṇa sādhayet//(p.271)
body.translated_text: 5.3.3. One who, without accepting the approach, still continues to meet — he should know her as being of divided mind. He should win her gradually.

body.text: 5.3.4/.apratigṛhya^abhiyogaṃ saviśeṣam alaṃkṛtā ca punar dṛśyeta tathā^eva tam abhigacchec ca vivikte balād grahaṇīyāṃ vidyāt//(p.271)
body.translated_text: 5.3.4. One who, without accepting the approach, appears again especially adorned and comes to him in a secluded place — he should know her as one to be seized by force.

body.text: 5.3.5/.bahūn api viṣa^hate +abhiyogān na ca cireṇa^api prayacchaty ātmānaṃ sā śuṣka^pratigrāhiṇī paricaya^vighaṭana^sādhyā//(p.272)
body.translated_text: 5.3.5. One who, even though she tolerates many approaches, does not yield herself even after a long time — she is a dry accepter (<s>śuṣkapratīgrāhiṇī</s>), to be won by breaking off the acquaintance.
5.3.6. Because of the inconstancy of the human mind.

body.text: 5.3.7/.abhiyukta^api pariharati/ na ca saṃsṛjyate/ na ca pratyācaṣṭe/ tasminn ātmani ca gaurava^abhimānāt/ sa^atiparicayāt kṛcchra^sādhyā/ marmajñayā dūtyā tāṃ sādhayet//(p.272)
body.translated_text: 5.3.7. One who, even when courted, avoids [him]; does not meet [him]; and does not refuse — through pride and self-regard in that person; and through excessive familiarity — she is difficult to win. He should win her through a female messenger who knows her vulnerabilities.
5.3.8. If she, when courted, rejects with harshness — she should be disregarded.
5.3.9. But one who, even after showing harshness, engages affectionately — she should be won.

body.text: 5.3.10/.kāraṇāt saṃsparśanaṃ sahate na^avabudhyate nāma dvidhā^bhūta^mānasā sātatyena kṣāntyā vā sādhyā/(p.273)
body.translated_text: 5.3.10. One who tolerates physical contact on some pretext, pretending not to notice — she is of divided mind and is to be won through persistence or patience.

body.text: 5.3.11/.samīpe śayānāyāḥ supto nāma karam upari vinyaset/ sāpi suptā^iva^upekṣate/ jāgratī tv apanuded bhūyo +abhiyoga^ākāṅkṣiṇī//(p.273)
body.translated_text: 5.3.11. When she lies nearby, he should, pretending to be asleep, place his hand upon her. If she too disregards it as if asleep — but when awake pushes it away while desiring further approach —
5.3.12. By this, the placing of a foot upon [her] foot is also explained.
5.3.13. When that has advanced further, he should begin the embrace while pretending to sleep.

body.text: 5.3.14/.tad^asahamānām utthitāṃ dvitīye +ahani prakṛti^vartinīm abhiyoga^arthinīṃ vidyāt/ adṛśyamānāṃ tu dūtī^sādhyām//(p.273)
body.translated_text: 5.3.14. If she does not tolerate it and rises, but on the second day behaves naturally and is seeking approach — he should know [her intent]. But if she is not seen [again], she is to be won through a messenger.

body.text: 5.3.15/.ciram adṛṣṭā^api prakṛtisthā^eva saṃsṛjyate kṛta^lakṣaṇāṃ tāṃ darśita^ākārām upakramet//(p.274)
body.translated_text: 5.3.15. Even one who has not been seen for a long time but meets again in her natural state — seeing her signs and displayed feelings, he should approach her.

body.text: 5.3.16/.anabhiyuktā^apy ākārayati/ vivikte ca^ātmānaṃ darśayati/ savepathu^gadgadaṃ vadati/ svinna^kara^caraṇa^aṅguliḥ svinna^mukhī ca bhavati/ śiraḥ^pīḍane saṃvāhane ca^ūrvor ātmānaṃ nāyake niyojayati/
body.translated_text: 5.3.16. Even without being courted, she signals; shows herself in a secluded place; speaks with trembling and stammering; her fingers of hand and foot become sweaty, and her face perspires; she engages the hero to press her head and massage her thighs.

body.text: 5.3.17/.āturā saṃvāhikā ca^ekena hastena saṃvāhayantī dvitīyena bāhunā sparśam āvedayati śleṣayati ca/ vismita^bhāvā/
body.translated_text: 5.3.17. Sick and being massaged, with one hand she massages [in return] and with the second arm she communicates and clings to [his] touch — with an expression of wonder.

body.text: 5.3.18/.nidrā^andhā vā parispṛśya^ūrubhyāṃ bāhubhyām api tiṣṭhati/ ali^kaika^deśam ūrvor upari pātayati/ ūrū^mūla^saṃvāhane niyuktā na pratilomayati/ tatra^eva hastam ekam avicalaṃ nyasyati/ aṅga^saṃdaṃśena ca pīḍitaṃ cirād apanayati/
body.translated_text: 5.3.18. Or, as if blinded by sleep, having touched [him], she remains [pressing against him] with her thighs and arms; she lets a small portion [of her body] fall upon his thighs; when engaged in massaging the base of the thighs, she does not resist; she places one hand there immovably; and when pressed by the grip of limbs, she removes [her hand] only after a long time.
5.3.19. Having thus accepted the hero's approaches, she comes again on the second day for massage.
5.3.20. She does not associate excessively, nor does she avoid [him].

body.text: 5.3.21/.vivikte bhāvaṃ darśayati niṣkāraṇaṃ ca^agūḍham anyatra pracchanna^pradeśāt/
body.translated_text: 5.3.21. She shows her feelings in private and without concealment, openly — except in a hidden place.

body.text: 5.3.22/.saṃnikṛṣṭa^paricāraka^upabhogyā sā ced ākāritā^api tathā^eva syāt sā marmajñayā dūtyā sādhyā/
body.translated_text: 5.3.22. If she, being accessible through a nearby attendant, even when signaled to, remains the same — she is to be won through a messenger who knows her vulnerabilities.

body.text: 5.3.23/.vyāvartamānā tu tarkaṇīyā^iti bhāva^parīkṣā//(p.274) bhavanti ca^atra ślokāḥ ---(p.275)
body.translated_text: 5.3.23. But one who turns away should be suspected — thus is the examination of feelings. And here there are verses:
5.3.24ab. First one should establish acquaintance, then conversation,
5.3.24cd. and mixed with conversation, the mutual communication of feelings.
5.3.25ab. If through her response one sees the acceptance of feelings,
5.3.25cd. then a man, free from timidity, should court the woman.
5.3.26ab. A woman who first conveys her own feelings through gestures —

body.text: 5.3.26cd/.kṣipram eva^abhiyojyā sā prathame tv eva darśane//(p.275)
body.translated_text: 5.3.26cd. she should be courted immediately, at the very first meeting.

body.text: 5.3.27ab/.ślakṣṇam ākāritā yā tu darśayet sphuṭam uttaram/(p.275)
body.translated_text: 5.3.27ab. But one who, when gently signaled to, shows a clear response —
5.3.27cd. she too should be known as ready at that very moment, being eager for love.
5.3.28ab. With a woman who is steadfast, slow-moving, bold,

body.text: 5.3.28cd/.eṣa sūkṣmo vidhiḥ proktaḥ siddhā eva sphuṭaṃ striyaḥ//(p.276)
body.translated_text: 5.3.28cd. and requiring examination — this subtle procedure has been taught; [for] women [already] won, [the approach is] obvious.
5.4. The Tasks of the Female Messenger (<s>dūtīkarmāṇi</s>)
5.4.1. A woman who has shown signs and gestures but is rarely seen, or who is new — he should approach through a female messenger.

body.text: 5.4.2/.sā^enāṃ śīlato +anupraviśya^ākhyāna^kapaṭaiḥ subhagaṃkaraṇa^yogair loka^vṛtta^antaiḥ kavi^kathābhiḥ pāra^dārika^kathābhiś ca tasyāś ca rūpa^vijñāna^dākṣiṇya^śīla^anupraśaṃsābhiś ca tāṃ rañjayet/
body.translated_text: 5.4.2. She [the messenger], entering [the woman's confidence] through her character, should charm her with narrative pretexts, with methods of making one attractive, with accounts of worldly affairs, with stories of poets, and with tales of others' wives — and with praises of her [the target woman's] beauty, knowledge, generosity, and character.

body.text: 5.4.3/.katham evaṃ vidhāyās tava^ayam ithaṃbhūtaḥ patir^iti ca^anuśayaṃ grāhayet/
body.translated_text: 5.4.3. [She should say:] 'How is it that one such as you has this kind of husband?' — and thus make her feel regret.

body.text: 5.4.4/.na tava subhage dāsyam api kartuṃ yukta iti brūyāt/
body.translated_text: 5.4.4. She should say: 'O fortunate one, it is not fitting for you to even serve [such a man].'

body.text: 5.4.5/.manda^vegatām īrṣyālutāṃ śaṭhatām akṛtajñatāṃ ca^asaṃbhoga^śīlatāṃ kadaryatāṃ capalatām anyāni ca yāni tasmin guptāny asyā abhyāśe sati sadbhāve +atiśayena bhāṣeta/
body.translated_text: 5.4.5. His slowness, jealousy, deceitfulness, ingratitude, lack of sexual engagement, miserliness, fickleness, and whatever other [faults] are hidden in him — in her [the woman's] presence, when there is trust, she should speak of these with great exaggeration.
5.4.6. And by whatever fault [the woman] is observed to be distressed — she should enter [her confidence] through that very [topic].
5.4.7. When she is a <s>mṛgī</s> (doe-woman, i.e., of delicate constitution), there is no fault of the <s>śaśa</s> (hare-man, i.e., a small-membered man).
5.4.8. By this same [principle], the case of the <s>vaḍavā</s> (mare-woman) and the <s>hastinī</s> (elephant-woman) is also explained.

body.text: 5.4.9/.nāyikāyā eva tu viśvāsyatām upalabhya dūtītvena^upasarpayet prathama^sāhasāyāṃ sūkṣma^bhāvāyāṃ ca^iti goṇikāputraḥ//(p.277)
body.translated_text: 5.4.9. But having ascertained that the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) herself is trustworthy, one should approach her as a messenger — in the case of one [venturing] for the first time and of subtle feelings — thus says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.

body.text:
5.4.10/.sā nāyakasya caritam anulomatāṃ kāmitāni ca kathayet/
5.4.11/.prasṛta^sad^bhāvāyāṃ ca yuktyā kārya^śarīram itthaṃ vadet/
body.translated_text: 5.4.10-11. She [the messenger] should tell of the hero's character, his agreeableness, and his desires. And when [the woman's] true feelings have advanced, she should skillfully speak the substance of the matter thus:

body.text: 5.4.12/.śṛṇu vicitram idaṃ subhage, tvāṃ kila dṛṣṭvā^amutra^asāv itthaṃ gotra^putro nāyakaś citta^unmādam anubhavati/ prakṛtyā sukumāraḥ kadā cid anyatra^aparikliṣṭa^pūrvas tapasvī/ tato +adhunā śakyam anena maraṇam apy anubhavitum iti varṇayet/
