body.text: 6.5.18/.kṛtajñas tu pūrva^śrama^apekṣī na sahasā virajyate/ parīkṣita^śīlatvāc ca na mithyā dūṣyata iti vātsyāyanaḥ//(p.345)
body.translated_text: 6.5.18. But a grateful one, considering past efforts, does not suddenly become dispassionate; and since his character has been tested, he is not falsely defamed — thus says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
6.5.19. Even there, distinction [is made] on the basis of future prospects.
6.5.20. Between the word of a friend and the arrival of wealth, the arrival of wealth has the evident advantage — say the teachers.

body.text: 6.5.21/.so +api hy artha^āgamo bhavitā/ mitraṃ tu sakṛd vākye pratihate kaluṣitaṃ syād iti vātsyāyanaḥ//(p.345)
body.translated_text: 6.5.21. That wealth too will come [eventually through the friend]; but a friend, once rebuffed in his request, may become alienated — thus says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
6.5.22. Even there, distinction [is made] on the basis of urgency.

body.text: 6.5.23/.tatra kārya^saṃdarśanena mitram anunīya śvobhūte vacanam astv iti tato +atipātinam arthaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt//(p.346)
body.translated_text: 6.5.23. There, having conciliated the friend by showing [him] the situation, [saying] 'let [your] request be [fulfilled] tomorrow,' she should accept the urgent wealth.
6.5.24. Between the arrival of wealth and the prevention of misfortune, the arrival of wealth has the evident advantage — say the teachers.

body.text: 6.5.25/.arthaḥ parimita^avacchedaḥ, anarthaḥ punaḥ sakṛt^prasṛto na jñāyate kva^avatiṣṭhata iti vātsyāyanaḥ//(p.346)
body.translated_text: 6.5.25. Wealth has a limited, definable extent; but a misfortune, once set in motion, one does not know where it will stop — thus says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
6.5.26. Even there, distinction [is made] on the basis of the gravity [of the matter].
6.5.27. By this, the advantage of preventing misfortune over a doubtful gain is explained.

body.text: 6.5.28/.devakula^taḍāga^ārāmāṇām karaṇam, sthalīnām agni^caityānāṃ nibandhanam, go^sahasrāṇāṃ pātra^antaritaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dānam, devatānāṃ pūjā^upahāra^pravartanam, tad^vyaya^sahiṣṇor vā dhanasya parigrahaṇam ity uttama^gaṇikānāṃ lābha^atiśayaḥ//(p.347)
body.translated_text: 6.5.28. The construction of temples, ponds, and gardens; the endowment of platforms, fire-altars, and <s>caityas</s> (shrines); the gift of thousands of cows, mediated by a vessel [i.e., through a Brāhmaṇa], to Brāhmaṇas; the establishment of worship-offerings to the deities; or the acquisition of wealth capable of bearing such expenditure — this is the supreme profit of the highest-class courtesans.

body.text: 6.5.29/.sārva^aṅgiko +alaṃkāra^yogo gṛhasya^udārasya karaṇam/ mahārhair bhāṇḍaiḥ paricārakaiś ca gṛha^paricchadasya^ujjvalata^iti rūpa^ājīvānāṃ lābhā^atiśayaḥ//(p.347)
body.translated_text: 6.5.29. Full bodily adornment, the making of a splendid house, and the brilliance of household furnishings with costly vessels and attendants — this is the supreme profit of those who live by their beauty.

body.text: 6.5.30/.nityaṃ śuklam ācchādanam apakṣudham anna^pānaṃ nityaṃ saugandhikena tāmbūlena ca yogaḥ sahiraṇya^bhāgam alaṃkaraṇam iti kumbha^dāsīnāṃ lābha^atiśayaḥ//(p.348)
body.translated_text: 6.5.30. Always wearing white garments, food and drink not meager, always using fragrant <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), and adornment including gold — this is the supreme profit of the <s>kumbhadāsī</s> (water-carrier courtesans).

body.text: 6.5.31/.etena pradeśena madhyama^adhamānām api lābha^atiśayān sarvāsām eva yojayed ity ācāryāḥ//(p.348)
body.translated_text: 6.5.31. By this principle, one should devise the supreme profits for the middle and lowest [classes of courtesans] as well — say the teachers.
6.5.32. The regulation of income and the like is not fixed, [but depends on] place, time, resources, capability, passion, and popular custom — thus says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

body.text:
6.5.33/.gamyam anyato nivārayitukāmā saktam anyasyām apahartukāmā vā anyāṃ vā lābhato viyuyukṣamāṇa^agamya^saṃsargād ātmanaḥ sthānaṃ vṛddhim āyatim abhigamyatāṃ ca manyamānā anartha^pratīkāre vā sāhāyam enaṃ kārayitukāmā saktasya vā ^anyasya vyalīka^arthinī pūrva^upakāram akṛtam iva paśyantī kevala prīty^arthinī vā kalyāṇa^buddher alpam api lābhaṃ
pratigṛhṇīyāt//(p.349)
body.translated_text: 6.5.33. Wishing to divert an [eligible client] from another; wishing to win one attached to another; wishing to separate another from gain; or considering that association with an ineligible one will [benefit] her own position, growth, future, and approachability; or wishing him to serve as an ally in preventing misfortune; or being hostile toward another who is attached [to him]; or seeing a past service as if undone; or desiring only affection from one of good intentions — she should accept even a small gain.

body.text: 6.5.34/.āyaty^arthinī tu tam āśritya ca^anarthaṃ praticikīrṣantī naiva pratigṛhṇīyāt//(p.349)
body.translated_text: 6.5.34. But one who desires future [gains], and relying on him intends to prevent misfortune — she should not accept at all [from someone who might compromise that].

body.text: 6.5.35/.tyakṣyāmy enam anyataḥ pratisaṃdhāsyāmi, gamiṣyati dārair yokṣyate nāśayiṣyaty anarthān, aṅkuśa^bhūta uttara^adhyakṣo +asya^āgamiṣyati svāmī pitā vā, sthāna^bhraṃśo vā^asya bhaviṣyati cala^cittaś ca^iti manyamānā tadātve tasmāl lābham icchet//(p.350)
body.translated_text: 6.5.35. [Thinking:] 'I will abandon him, I will make arrangements elsewhere; he will go away, he will take a wife, he will ruin my fortunes; a restraining higher authority — his master or father — will come; or his position will collapse, and he is fickle-minded' — thinking thus, she should seek gain from him immediately.

body.text: 6.5.36/.pratijñātam īśvareṇa pratigrahaṃ lapsyate adhikaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ vā prāpsyati vṛtti^kālo +asya vā āsannaḥ vāhanam asyā gamiṣyati sthala^pattraṃ vā sasyam asya pakṣyate kṛtam asmin na naśyati nityam avisaṃvādako vā^ity āyatyām icchet/ parigraha^kalpaṃ vā^ācaret//(p.350) bhavanti ca^atra ślokāḥ---(p.351)
body.translated_text: 6.5.36. [Thinking:] 'What was promised will be received from the lord; he will obtain a position or authority; the time of his employment is near; his vehicle will come to her; the grain on his land will ripen; [favors] done for him will not be lost; or he is always truthful' — she should seek [gains] in the future. Or she should behave as if she were a wife. And here are verses:
6.5.37ab. Those whose wealth is hard-won, those who are favorites of the king [and therefore] cruel,

body.text: 6.5.37cd/.āyātyāṃ ca tadātve ca dūrād eva vivarjayet//(p.351)
body.translated_text: 6.5.37cd. both for the future and the present, she should avoid from afar.
6.5.38ab. Those from whom avoidance brings misfortune and approach brings prosperity —
6.5.38cd. she should seize them even with effort, with a suitable pretext.
6.5.39ab. Those who are pleased and give immeasurable wealth even for a trifle,

body.text: 6.5.39cd/.sthūla^lakṣān mahotsāhāṃs tān gacchet svair api vyayaiḥ//(p.351)
body.translated_text: 6.5.39cd. generous and of great enthusiasm — she should go to them even at her own expense.
6.6 [Chapter on the assessment of gains, losses, consequences, and doubts, and on special types of courtesans]:

body.text: 6.6.1/.arthān ācaryamāṇān anarthā apy anūdbhavanty anubandhāḥ saṃśayāś ca//(p.352)
body.translated_text: 6.6.1. When gains are being pursued, losses, consequences, and doubts also arise.

body.text: 6.6.2/.te buddhi^daurbalyād atirāgād atyabhimānād atidambhād atyārjavād ativiśvāsād atikrodhāt pramādāt sāhasād daivayogāc ca syuḥ//(p.352)
body.translated_text: 6.6.2. These [arise] from weakness of judgment, excessive passion, excessive pride, excessive deceit, excessive straightforwardness, excessive trust, excessive anger, carelessness, recklessness, and the workings of fate.

body.text: 6.6.3/.teṣāṃ phalaṃ kṛtasya vyayasya niṣphalatvam anāyatirāgam iṣyato +arthasya nivartanam āptasya niṣkramaṇaṃ pāruṣyasya prāptir gamyatā śarīrasya (p.352)praghātaḥ keśānāṃ chedanaṃ pātanam aṅga^vaikalyā^pattiḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.3. Their results are: the fruitlessness of expenditure already made; loss of future passion; the reverting of desired wealth; the departure of what was obtained; the incurring of harshness; loss of approachability; injury to the body; cutting of hair; [causing one to] fall; and the occurrence of bodily disfigurement.

body.text: 6.6.4/.tasmāt tān ādita eva parijihīrṣed arthabhūyiṣṭhāṃś ca^upekṣeta//(p.353)
body.translated_text: 6.6.4. Therefore, she should try to avoid these from the very beginning, and should disregard those that are overwhelmingly material.
6.6.5. Gain, <s>dharma</s> (merit), and <s>kāma</s> (love) — this is the triad of gains.
6.6.6. Loss, <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and hatred — this is the triad of losses.
6.6.7. When these are being pursued, the arising of another as well is a consequence (<s>anubandha</s>).

body.text: 6.6.8/.saṃdigdhāyāṃ tu phala^prāptau syād vā na vā^iti śuddha^saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.8. When the attainment of a result is doubtful — 'it will happen or it will not' — this is a simple doubt.
6.6.9. 'This will happen or that will happen' — this is a mixed [doubt].
6.6.10. When, in performing one action, two results arise — this is a conjunction from both sides.
6.6.11. When results arise from all sides — this is a conjunction from all sides. We shall illustrate these.
6.6.12. The triad of gains takes the form of what has been examined. The triad of losses is simply its opposite.

body.text: 6.6.13/.yasya^uttamasya^abhigamane pratyakṣato +artha^lābho grahaṇīyatvam āyatir āgamaḥ prārthanīyatvaṃ ca^anyeṣāṃ syāt so +artho +artha^anubandhaḥ//(p.354)
body.translated_text: 6.6.13. When approaching a superior [client], there is visible gain, acceptability, future [benefit], income, desirability by others — that is a gain with [positive] consequences.

body.text: 6.6.14/.lābha^mātre kasya cid anyasya gamanaṃ so +artho niranubandhaḥ//(p.354)
body.translated_text: 6.6.14. Going to someone merely for a single gain — that is a gain without consequences.

body.text: 6.6.15/.anya^artha^parigrahe saktād āyati^cchedanam arthasya niṣkramaṇaṃ loka^vidviṣṭasya vā nīcasya gamanam āyatighnam artho +anartha^anubandhaḥ//(p.354)
body.translated_text: 6.6.15. When, from accepting the wealth of someone attached [to another], there is the cutting off of future [prospects], the departure of wealth, or the going to one who is hated by the public or low — a gain that destroys future [prospects] is a gain with [negative] consequences.

body.text: 6.6.16/.(svena vyayena śūrasya mahāmātrasya prabhavato vā lubdhasya gamanaṃ niṣphalam api vyasana^pratīkāra^arthaṃ mahataś ca^arthaghnasya nimittasya praśamanam āyati^jananaṃ vā so +anartho +artha^anubandhaḥ//)(p.355)
body.translated_text: 6.6.16. Going at one's own expense to a hero, a high official, or a powerful but miserly person — though fruitless, if it serves to counteract a calamity or to pacify a great wealth-destroying cause or to generate future [prospects] — that is a loss with [positive] consequences.

body.text: 6.6.17/.kadaryasya subhaga^māninaḥ kṛtaghnasya vā^atisaṃdhāna^śīlasya svair api vyayais tathā^ārādhanam ante niṣphalaṃ so +anartho niranubandhaḥ//(p.355)
body.translated_text: 6.6.17. Serving a miser, one who considers himself fortunate, an ungrateful one, or one disposed to cheating — even at one's own expense — which ends fruitlessly: that is a loss without consequences.

body.text: 6.6.18/.tasya^eva rāja^vallabhasya kraurya^prabhāva^adhikasya tathā^eva^ārādhanam ante niṣphalaṃ niṣkāsanaṃ ca doṣa^karaṃ so +anartho +anartha^anubandhaḥ//(p.355)
body.translated_text: 6.6.18. Serving in the same way one who is a favorite of the king, whose cruelty and power are excessive — which ends fruitlessly, and whose expulsion would cause harm: that is a loss with [further] negative consequences.
6.6.19. Thus one should also devise consequences for <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>.
6.6.20. And one should combine them with each other by reasoning — these are the consequences.
6.6.21. 'Even if pleased, will he give or not?' — this is a doubt about gain.

body.text: 6.6.22/.niṣpīḍita^artham aphalam utsṛjantyā artham alabhamānāyā dharmaḥ syān na vā^iti dharma^saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.22. 'If I abandon one who has been squeezed of wealth and is fruitless, without obtaining gain, will there be merit or not?' — this is a doubt about <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: 6.6.23/.abhipretam upalabhya paricārakam anyaṃ vā kṣudraṃ gatvā kāmaḥ syān na vā^iti kāma^saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.23. 'Having found one who is desirable, if I go to an attendant or another lowly person, will there be pleasure or not?' — this is a doubt about <s>kāma</s>.
6.6.24. 'A powerful but lowly and undesirable person — will he cause misfortune or not?' — this is a doubt about loss.

body.text: 6.6.25/.atyanta^niṣphalaḥ saktaḥ parityaktaḥ pitṛ^lokaṃ yāyāt tatra^adharmaḥ syān na vā^ity adharma^saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.25. 'One who is utterly fruitless, attached — if abandoned, he would go to the other world [i.e., die]; would there be demerit or not?' — this is a doubt about <s>adharma</s>.

body.text: 6.6.26/.rāgasya^api vivakṣāyām abhipretam anupalabhya virāgaḥ/ syān na vā^iti dveṣa^saṃśayaḥ/ iti śuddha^saṃśayāḥ//(p.356)
body.translated_text: 6.6.26. 'Even when [there is] a desire to express passion, not finding one who is desirable — will there be aversion or not?' — this is a doubt about hatred. These are the simple doubts.
6.6.27. Now, the mixed [doubts]:

body.text: 6.6.28/.āgantor avidita^śīlasya vallabha^saṃśrayasya prabhaviṣṇor vā samupasthitasya^ārādhanam artho +anartha iti saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.28. The courting of a stranger of unknown character, who has the support of a powerful person, or who is himself powerful and has presented himself — 'will it be gain or loss?' — this is a mixed doubt.

body.text: 6.6.29/.śrotriyasya brahmacāriṇo dīkṣitasya vratino liṅgino vā māṃ dṛṣṭvā jāta^rāgasya mumūrṣor mitra^vākyād ānṛśaṃsyāc ca gamanaṃ dharmo +adharma iti saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.29. Going, on the word of a friend or out of compassion, to a <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar), a celibate student, an initiated person, one who has undertaken a vow, or an ascetic who, having seen her, has become impassioned and is about to die — 'will it be merit or demerit?' — this is a [mixed] doubt.

body.text: 6.6.30/.lokād eva^ākṛta^pratyayād aguṇo guṇavān vā^ity anavekṣya gamanaṃ kāmo dveṣa iti saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.30. Going, without ascertaining [whether he is] virtuous or not, to one about whom public opinion alone has been formed — 'will it be pleasure or hatred?' — this is a [mixed] doubt.
6.6.31. And one should combine these with each other — these are the mixed doubts.

body.text: 6.6.32/.yatra parasya^abhigamane +arthaḥ saktāc ca saṃgharṣataḥ sa ubhayayo +arthaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.32. Where in approaching another there is gain, and from the attached [current client] too there is gain through friction — that is gain from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.33/.yatra svena vyayena niṣphalam abhigamanaṃ saktāc ca^amarṣitād vitta^pratyādānaṃ sa ubhayato +anarthaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.33. Where the approach at one's own expense is fruitless, and from the angered attached one there is recovery of wealth — that is loss from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.34/.yatra^abhigamane +artho bhaviṣyati na vā^ity āśaṅkā sakto +api saṃgharṣād dāsyati na vā^iti sa ubhayato +artha^saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.34. Where in approaching [someone], 'there will be gain or not' is the apprehension, and 'the attached one too, through friction, will give or not' — that is a doubt about gain from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.35/.yatra^abhigamane vyayavati pūrvo viruddhaḥ krodhād apakāraṃ kariṣyati na vā^iti sakto vāmarṣito dattaṃ pratyādāsyati na vā^iti sa ubhayato +anarthasaṃśayaḥ/ ity auddālaker ubhayato^yogāḥ//(p.358)
body.translated_text: 6.6.35. Where in approaching [a new client] at one's own expense, the previous one who is hostile may or may not cause harm out of anger, or the attached and resentful one will or will not demand back what was given — that is a doubt about loss from both sides. Thus [end] the conjunctions from both sides according to <s>Auddālaki</s>.
6.6.36. But the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s> [say]:
6.6.37. Where in approaching there is gain, and in not approaching there is also gain from the attached one — that is gain from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.38/.yatra^abhigamane niṣphalo vyayo +anabhigamane ca niṣpratī^kāro +anarthaḥ sa ubhayato +anarthaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.38. Where in approaching the expenditure is fruitless, and in not approaching there is irremediable loss [from the attached one's anger] — that is loss from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.39/.yatra^abhigamane nirvyayo dāsyati na vā^iti saṃśayo +anabhigamane sakto dāsyati na vā^iti sa ubhayato +artha^saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.39. Where in approaching without expense, 'he will give or not' is the apprehension, and in not approaching, 'the attached one will give or not' — that is a doubt about gain from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.40/.yatra^abhigamane vyayavati pūrvo viruddhaḥ prabhāvavān prāpsyate na vā^iti saṃśayo +anabhigamane ca krodhād anarthaṃ kariṣyati na vā^iti sa ubhayato +anartha^saṃśayaḥ//(p.359)
body.translated_text: 6.6.40. Where in approaching at one's own expense, the previous hostile and powerful one 'will recover [the wealth] or not' is the apprehension, and in not approaching, 'he will or will not cause harm out of anger' — that is a doubt about loss from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.41/.eteṣām eva vyatikare +anyato +artho +anyato +anarthaḥ, anyato +artho +anyato +artha^saṃśayaḥ, anyato +artho +anyato +anartha^saṃśaya iti ṣaṭsaṃkīrṇa^yogāḥ//(p.360)
body.translated_text: 6.6.41. In combinations of these same [types]: gain from one side and loss from the other; gain from one side and doubt about gain from the other; gain from one side and doubt about loss from the other — these are the six mixed conjunctions.

body.text: 6.6.42/.teṣu sahāyaiḥ saha vimṛśya yato +artha^bhūyiṣṭho +artha^saṃśayo gurur anartha^praśamo vā tataḥ pravarteta//(p.360)
body.translated_text: 6.6.42. Among these, having deliberated with her associates, she should proceed where gain is greatest, or where the doubt about gain is weighty, or where the loss is pacifiable.

body.text: 6.6.43/.evaṃ dharma^kāmav apy anayā^eva yuktyā^udāharet/ saṃkirec ca paraspareṇa vyatiṣañjayec ca^ity ubhayato^yogāḥ//(p.360)
body.translated_text: 6.6.43. In the same way, one should illustrate <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> by this very reasoning; and one should combine them with each other and interlink them — these are the conjunctions from both sides.

body.text: 6.6.44/.saṃbhūya ca viṭāḥ parigṛhṇanty ekām asau goṣṭhī^parigrahaḥ/
body.translated_text: 6.6.44. And when <s>viṭas</s> (libertines) collectively maintain a single [courtesan] — that is the collective maintenance (<s>goṣṭhī-parigraha</s>).

body.text: 6.6.45/.sā teṣām itas tataḥ saṃsṛjyamānā pratyekaṃ saṃgharṣād arthaṃ nirvartayet/
body.translated_text: 6.6.45. She, being shared among them here and there, should extract wealth from each through their mutual rivalry.

body.text: 6.6.46/.suvasantaka^ādiṣu ca yoge yo me imam amuṃ ca saṃpādayiṣyati tasya^ādya gamiṣyati me duhitā^iti mātrā vācayet/
body.translated_text: 6.6.46. And at [festivals like] <s>Suvasantaka</s> and the like, she should have her mother announce: 'Whoever will procure this and that for me — to him my daughter will go tonight.'
6.6.47. And in approaches arising from their rivalry, she should note the profitable opportunities.

body.text: 6.6.48/.ekato +arthaḥ sarvato +arthaḥ ekato +anarthaḥ sarvato +anarthaḥ ardhato +arthaḥ sarvato +arthaḥ ardhato +anarthaḥ sarvato +anarthaḥ/ iti samantato yogāḥ//(p.362)
body.translated_text: 6.6.48. Gain from one is gain from all; loss from one is loss from all; gain from a portion is gain from all; loss from a portion is loss from all — these are the conjunctions from all sides.

body.text: 6.6.49/.artha^saṃśayam anartha^saṃśayaṃ ca pūrvavad yojayet/ saṃkirec ca tathā dharma^kāmāv api/ ity *anubandha^artha^anartha[ch:artha^anartha^anubandha]^saṃśaya^vicārāḥ//(p.363)
body.translated_text: 6.6.49. Doubt about gain and doubt about loss should be connected as before; and <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> should be combined likewise. Thus [end] the considerations regarding consequences, gains, losses, and doubts.

body.text: 6.6.50/.kumbha^dāsī paricārikā kulaṭā svairiṇī naṭī śilpa^kārikā prakāśa^vinaṣṭā rūpa^ājīvā gaṇikā ca^iti veśyā^viśeṣāḥ//(p.363)
body.translated_text: 6.6.50. A <s>kumbhadāsī</s> (water-carrier), a <s>paricārikā</s> (attendant), a <s>kulaṭā</s> (unchaste woman), a <s>svairiṇī</s> (independent woman), a <s>naṭī</s> (actress), a <s>śilpakārikā</s> (craftswoman), an openly ruined woman (<s>prakāśavinaṣṭā</s>), one who lives by her beauty (<s>rūpājīvā</s>), and a <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) — these are the special types of courtesans.

body.text: 6.6.51/.sarvāsāṃ ca^anurūpeṇa gamyāḥ sahāyās tad uparañjanam artha^āgama^upāyā niṣkāsanaṃ punaḥ sadhānaṃ lābha^viśeṣa^anubandhā artha^anartha^anubandha^saṃśaya^vicārāś ca^iti vaiśikam//(p.363) bhavataś ca^atra ślokau ---(p.364)
body.translated_text: 6.6.51. For all of them: suitable clients, their associates, ways to please them, means of acquiring wealth, methods of dismissal, means of reunion, distinctions in profit along with their consequences, and considerations regarding gains, losses, consequences, and doubts — this constitutes the [section on] courtesans (<s>vaiśika</s>). And here are two verses:
6.6.52ab. Men desire women for pleasure, and women too desire [men] for pleasure;
6.6.52cd. since the teaching is primarily focused on wealth, therefore the instruction here is for women.
6.6.53ab. There are women devoted to passion, and there are also women devoted to wealth;

body.text: 6.6.53cd/.prāk tatra varṇito rāgo veśyā^yogāś ca vaiśike//(p.364)
body.translated_text: 6.6.53cd. passion has been described earlier, while the means for courtesans [are described] in the <s>vaiśika</s> [section].
7. The Secret Chapter (<s>Aupaniṣadika</s>)
7.1. Making oneself attractive (<s>subhagaṃkaraṇa</s>), subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>), and aphrodisiac preparations (<s>vṛṣya yogas</s>)
7.1.1. The <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been expounded.

body.text: 7.1.2/.tatra^uktais tu vidhibhir abhipretam artham anadhigacchan *aupaniṣadikam[ch:upaniṣadikam] ācaret/
body.translated_text: 7.1.2. When one does not attain the desired object by the methods stated therein, one should resort to the secret practices (<s>aupaniṣadika</s>).
7.1.3. Beauty, virtues, youth, and generosity — these are [natural means of] making oneself attractive (<s>subhagaṃkaraṇa</s>).
7.1.4. An ointment of <s>tagara</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>tālīsa-patraka</s> is [a means of] making oneself attractive.

body.text: 7.1.5/.etair eva supiṣṭair vartim ālipya^akṣatailena naraka^pāle sādhitam añjanaṃ ca/
body.translated_text: 7.1.5. With these same [substances] finely ground, making a wick and anointing it with uncooked sesame oil, [and then] preparing a collyrium in a skull — [this is another means].
7.1.6. An oil prepared with the leaves of <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>, and <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) [is an] anointing [preparation for attractiveness].
7.1.7. And garlands combined with those [same substances].

body.text: 7.1.8/.padma^utpala^nāgakesarāṇāṃ śoṣitānāṃ cūrṇaṃ madhu^ghṛtābhyām avalihya subhago bhavati/
body.translated_text: 7.1.8. Having licked the powder of dried <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and <s>nāgakesara</s> (mesua) mixed with honey and ghee, one becomes attractive.
7.1.9. Those same [substances] combined with <s>tagara</s>, <s>tālīsa</s>, and <s>tamāla-patra</s> [serve as] an ointment.

body.text: 7.1.10/.mayūrasya^akṣitarakṣor vā suvarṇena^*ālipya[ch:avalipya] dakṣiṇa^hastena dhārayed iti subhagaṃ^karaṇam/
body.translated_text: 7.1.10. Having coated the eye of a peacock or a <s>tarakṣu</s> (hyena) with gold, one should carry it on the right hand — this is a means of making oneself attractive.

body.text: 7.1.11/.tathā *bādaraṃ maṇiṃ[ch:bādaramaṇiṃ] śaṅkha^maṇiṃ ca teṣāṃ [ch inserts, tathā^eva teṣu]ca^ātharvaṇān yogān gamayet/
body.translated_text: 7.1.11. Likewise a <s>bādara</s> (jujube) gem and a conch gem — and one should apply to them the rites from the <s>Atharvaṇa</s> [Veda].

body.text: 7.1.12/.vidyā^tantrāc ca vidyā^yogāt prāpta^yauvanāṃ paricārikāṃ svāmī saṃvatsara^mātram anyato *dhārayet[ch:vārayet]/ tato *dhāritāṃ[ch:vāritāṃ] bālāṃ *matvā[ch:vāmatvāl] lālasī^bhūteṣu gamyeṣu yo +a*asyāḥ[ch:asyai] *saṃha(gha)rṣeṇa[ch:saṃgharṣeṇa] bahu dadyāt tasmai visṛjed iti saubhāgya^vardhanam/
body.translated_text: 7.1.12. Through the science of arts and the application of [that] knowledge, a master should keep a maidservant who has reached puberty away [from others] for just one year. Then, having kept the young [girl] restrained, when the desirable [clients] have become eager, to whichever one would give much through rivalry for her — to him she should be released. This is a means of increasing good fortune.

body.text: 7.1.13/.gaṇikā prāpta^yauvanāṃ svāṃ duhitaraṃ tasyā vijñāna^śīla^rūpa^anurūpyeṇa tān abhinimantrya sāreṇa yo *+asyai[ch:+asya] idam idaṃ ca dadyāt sa pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīyād iti *saṃsādhya[ch:saṃbhāṣya] rakṣayed iti/
body.translated_text: 7.1.13. A <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) should invite suitable persons — matching her daughter who has reached youth in knowledge, character, and beauty — and negotiate: 'Whoever gives this and that to her, he shall take her hand [in a formal arrangement]' — and thus protect her.

body.text: 7.1.14/.sā ca mātura^viditā nāma nāgarika^putrair dhanibhir atyarthaṃ prīyeta/
body.translated_text: 7.1.14. And she, with her mother's tacit knowledge, should be especially pleased with the wealthy sons of urbane men.

body.text: 7.1.15/.teṣāṃ kalā^grahaṇe gandharva^śālāyāṃ bhikṣukī^bhavane tatra tatra ca saṃdarśana^yogāḥ/
body.translated_text: 7.1.15. Opportunities for meeting them arise at music schools, in the <s>gandharva</s>-hall, at the residence of the mendicant woman, and at various [other places].
7.1.16. The mother should give her hand [in arrangement] to the one among them who gives as promised.

body.text: 7.1.17/.*tat[ch:om.] tāvad artham alabhamānā tu svena^apy ekadeśena *duhitre[ch:duhitra] etad dattam anena^iti khyāpayet/ [ch:ins.7.1.18/.ūḍhāyā vā kanyābhāvaṃ vimocayet//]
body.translated_text: 7.1.17. But if she does not obtain the [promised] amount, she should even from her own resources publicize: 'This has been given to my daughter by him.'

body.text: 7.1.19/.pracchannaṃ vā taiḥ saṃyojya svayam ajānatī bhūtvā tato viditeṣv *evaṃ[ch:etaṃ] dharmastheṣu nivedayet/
body.translated_text: 7.1.19. Or, having secretly united [her] with them, the [mother] herself pretending ignorance, should then report to recognized arbiters of law.

body.text: 7.1.20/.sakhyā^eva tu dāsyā vā mocita^kanyā^*bhāvām upagṛhīta[ch:bhāvāṃ sugṛhāta]^kāmasūtrām ābhyāsikeṣu yogeṣu pratiṣṭhitāṃ pratiṣṭhite(p.365)vayasi saubhāgye ca duhitaram avasṛjanti gaṇikā iti *prāpya[ch:prācya]^upacārāḥ/
body.translated_text: 7.1.20. Courtesans release their daughter — whose maidenhood has been freed by a friend or maidservant, who has been trained in the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>, who is established in the relevant practices, and who is established in [appropriate] age and good fortune — [into the profession]. These are the customary practices.

body.text: 7.1.21/.pāṇi^grahaś ca saṃvatsaram avyabhicāryas tato yathā kāminī syāt/
body.translated_text: 7.1.21. And the formal hand-taking [arrangement] requires exclusivity for one year; after that she may behave as she pleases.

body.text: 7.1.22/.ūrdhvam api saṃvatsarāt pariṇītena nimantryamāṇā lābham apy utsṛjya tāṃ rātriṃ tasya^āgacched iti veśyāyāḥ *pāṇi[ch:pāṇa]^grahaṇa^vidhiḥ saubhāgya^vardhanaṃ ca/
body.translated_text: 7.1.22. Even after more than a year, when invited by the married [client], abandoning even [other] gain, she should go to him for that night — this is the rule of the courtesan's formal arrangement, and a means of increasing good fortune.
7.1.23. By this, the daughters of those who live by the stage [performers] are also explained.

body.text: 7.1.24/.tasmai tu tāṃ dadyur ya eṣāṃ *tūryaviśiṣṭam[ch:tūrye viśiṣṭam] upakuryāt/ iti subhagaṃ^karaṇam/ (ekonaṣaṣṭitamaṃ prakaraṇam//)(p.366)
body.translated_text: 7.1.24. They should give her to the one who would especially assist them in their art. Thus [ends the section on] making oneself attractive. (The fifty-ninth topic.)
7.1.25. Applying to the member a mixture of powdered <s>dhattūraka</s> (datura), pepper, and long pepper with honey, and then engaging in intercourse — this is <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s> (subjugation).
7.1.26. A leaf blown by the wind, the remains from a funeral offering, and peacock bone-powder sprinkled [on the person] — this is <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.27/.svayaṃ^mṛtāyā maṇḍala^kārikāyāś cūrṇaṃ madhu^saṃyuktaṃ saha^āmalakaiḥ snānaṃ vaśī^karaṇam/
body.translated_text: 7.1.27. The powder of a <s>maṇḍalakārikā</s> (a type of insect/creature) that has died naturally, mixed with honey, [used as] a bath along with <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) — this is <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.28/.vajra^snuhī^gaṇḍakāni khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtāni manaḥśilā^gandha^pāṣāṇa^cūrṇena^abhyajya sapta^kṛtvaḥ śoṣitāni cūrṇayitvā madhunā lipta^liṅgasya saṃprayogo vaśī^karaṇam/
body.translated_text: 7.1.28. The galls of the <s>vajra-snuhī</s> (cactus spurge) plant, cut into pieces, anointed with the powder of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) and <s>gandha-pāṣāṇa</s> (sulphur stone), dried seven times, powdered, and applied to the member with honey — intercourse [with this] is <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.29/.etena^eva rātrau dhūmaṃ kṛtvā tad^dhūma^tiraskṛtaṃ sauvarṇaṃ candramasaṃ darśayati/
body.translated_text: 7.1.29. With these same [substances], making a fumigation at night, one shows the golden moon obscured by that smoke.

body.text: 7.1.30/.etair eva cūrṇitair vānara^purīṣa^miśritair yāṃ kanyām avakiret sa^anyasmai na dīyate/
body.translated_text: 7.1.30. With these same [substances] powdered and mixed with monkey dung, whatever maiden is sprinkled — she is not given to another.

body.text: 7.1.31/.vacā^gaṇḍakāni sahakāra^taila^liptāni śiṃśapā^vṛkṣa^skandham utkīrya [ch inserts, ṣaṇmāsaṃ] nidadhyāt/ [ch inserts, tataḥ] ṣaḍbhir māsair apanītāni deva^kāntam anulepanaṃ vaśī^karaṇaṃ ca^ity ācakṣate/
body.translated_text: 7.1.31. Galls of <s>vacā</s> (calamus), anointed with mango oil, should be placed [for six months] in a hollowed-out trunk of a <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree. After six months, having removed them — they say it is an ointment called <s>devakānta</s> (beloved of the gods) and a means of <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.32/.tathā khadira^sārajāni śakalāni tanūni yaṃ vṛkṣam utkīrya [ch inserts, ṣaṇmāsaṃ] nidadhyāt tat^puṣpa^gandhāni bhavanti/ gandharva^kāntam anulepanaṃ vaśī^karaṇaṃ ca^ity ācakṣate
body.translated_text: 7.1.32. Likewise, thin chips of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) heartwood, which, placed in a hollowed-out tree [for six months], become fragrant like flowers — they say it is an ointment called <s>gandharvakānta</s> (beloved of the <s>Gandharvas</s>) and a means of <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.33/.priyaṃgavas tagara^miśrāḥ sahakāra^taila^digdhā *nāgakesara[ch:nāga]^vṛkṣam utkīrya *ṣaṇmāsa[ch:ṣaṇmāsaṃ]^nihitā nāga^kāntam anulepanaṃ vaśī^karaṇam ity ācakṣate/
body.translated_text: 7.1.33. <s>Priyaṅgu</s> (callicarpa) [berries] mixed with <s>tagara</s>, smeared with mango oil, placed for six months in a hollowed-out <s>nāgakesara</s> tree — they say it is an ointment called <s>nāgakānta</s> (beloved of the <s>Nāgas</s>) and a means of <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.34/.*uṣṭrasya[ch:uṣṭra]^asthi bhṛṅgarāja^rasena bhāvitaṃ dagdham *añjanam uṣṭra^asthy *añjanikāyāṃ[ch:añjanaṃ nalikāyāṃ] nihitam uṣṭra^asthi^śalākayā^eva sroto +añjana^sahitaṃ puṇyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ vaśī^karaṇaṃ ca^ity ācakṣate/
body.translated_text: 7.1.34. The bone of a camel, steeped in the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (eclipta) and then burned, [makes] a collyrium; placed in a tube of camel bone, with a camel-bone applicator — they say it is auspicious, good for the eyes, and a means of <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>.

body.text: 7.1.35/.etena śyena^bhāsa^mayūra^asthi^mayāny añjanāni vyākhātāni/ (iti vaśī^karaṇam/ ṣaṣṭitamaṃ prakaraṇam//)(p.366)
body.translated_text: 7.1.35. By this, collyria made from the bones of hawks, eagles, and peacocks are [also] explained. (Thus [ends] <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>. The sixtieth topic.)

body.text: 7.1.36/.uccaṭākandaś *ca[ch:cavyā] yaṣṭīmadhukaṃ ca saśarkareṇa payasā pītvā *vṛṣo[ch:vṛṣī] bhavati/
body.translated_text: 7.1.36. Having drunk the root of <s>uccaṭā</s> (a plant) and <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s> (licorice) with milk and sugar, one becomes virile.
7.1.37. Drinking milk boiled with the testicles of a ram or goat, with sugar — this is an aphrodisiac preparation.
7.1.38. Likewise, drinking with milk [a preparation of] <s>vidārī</s> (pueraria), <s>kṣīrikā</s>, and <s>svayaṃguptā</s> (mucuna pruriens).
7.1.39. Likewise, [the seeds of] <s>piyāla</s> (buchanania), <s>moraṭā</s>, and <s>vidārī</s> — with milk alone.

body.text: 7.1.40/.śṛṅgāṭaka^kaseru^*madhūkāni[ch:kāma^dhūlikāni] kṣīrakākolyā saha piṣṭāni saśarkareṇa payasā ghṛtena manda^agninā^utkarikāṃ paktvā yāvad arthaṃ bhakṣitavān anantāḥ striyo gacchati^ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/
body.translated_text: 7.1.40. <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water chestnut), <s>kaseru</s> (scirpus), and <s>madhūka</s> (bassia), ground together with <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, cooked over a gentle fire with milk and sugar and ghee into a cake — having eaten as much as needed, one goes to innumerable women, so they say.

body.text:
7.1.41/.māṣaka^malinīṃ payasā dhautām uṣṇena ghṛtena mṛdūkṛtya^uddhṛtāṃ vṛddha^vatsāyāḥ goḥ payaḥ siddhaṃ pāyasaṃ madhu^sarpirbhyām aśitvā^+anantāḥ striyo gacchati^ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/
7.1.42/.vidārī svayaṃguptā śarkarā^madhu^sarpirbhyāṃ godhūma^cūrṇena polikāṃ kṛtvā yāvad arthaṃ bhakṣitavān anantāḥ striyo gacchati^ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/
body.translated_text: 7.1.41. A <s>māṣa</s> bean-soiled [cloth], washed in milk, softened with hot ghee, then removed — [from this, cooking] a milk-pudding with the milk of a cow whose calf has matured, and eating it with honey and ghee, one goes to innumerable women, so they say. 7.1.42. Making a cake of <s>vidārī</s> and <s>svayaṃguptā</s> with sugar, honey, ghee, and wheat flour — having eaten as much as needed, one goes to innumerable women, so they say.

body.text: 7.1.43/.caṭaka^aṇḍa^rasa^bhāvitais taṇḍulaiḥ pāyasaṃ siddhaṃ madhu^sarpirbhyāṃ plāvitaṃ yāvad artham iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa/
body.translated_text: 7.1.43. A milk-pudding cooked with rice steeped in the juice of sparrow eggs, drizzled with honey and ghee, [eaten] as much as needed — this is the same as the previous [formula].

body.text: 7.1.44/.caṭaka^aṇḍa^rasa^bhāvitān apagatatvacas tilān śṛṅgāṭaka^kaseruka^svayaṃguptā^phalāni godhūma^māṣa^cūrṇaiḥ saśarkareṇa payasā sarpiṣā ca pakvaṃ *pāyasaṃ[ch:saṃyāvaṃ] yāvad arthaṃ *prāśitam[ch:prāśitavān] iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa/
body.translated_text: 7.1.44. Sesame seeds with husks removed, steeped in sparrow-egg juice, [combined with] <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, <s>kaseruka</s>, and <s>svayaṃguptā</s> fruits, cooked with wheat and <s>māṣa</s> flour, milk with sugar, and ghee into a pudding — eaten as much as needed, this is the same as the previous [formula].

body.text: 7.1.45/.sarpiṣo madhunaḥ śarkarāyā madhukasya ca dve dve pale madhu^rasāyāḥ karṣaḥ prasthaṃ payasa iti ṣaḍ^aṅgam amṛtaṃ medhyaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyaṃ yukta^rasam ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/
body.translated_text: 7.1.45. Two <s>palas</s> each of ghee, honey, sugar, and bee's honey, one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>madhurasa</s> (grape juice), and one <s>prastha</s> of milk—[this] six-ingredient [preparation called] <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) is [said to be] beneficial for the intellect, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and of balanced flavor—so they declare.

body.text: 7.1.46/.śatāvarī^śvadaṃṣṭrā^guḍa^kaṣāye pippalī^madhu^kalke go^kṣīra^cchāga^ghṛte pakve tasya puṣpa[ch:puṣya]^ārambheṇa^anvahaṃ prāśanaṃ medhyaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyaṃ yukta^rasam ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/
body.translated_text: 7.1.46. A decoction of <s>śatāvarī</s> (asparagus) and <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (tribulus) with jaggery, [combined with] a paste of <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) and honey, cooked in cow's milk and goat's ghee—the daily consumption of this, beginning on [the day of the constellation] <s>Puṣya</s>, is beneficial for the intellect, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and of balanced flavor—so they declare.

body.text: 7.1.47/.śatāvaryāḥ śvadaṃṣṭrāyāḥ śrīparṇī^phalānāṃ ca kṣuṇṇānāṃ catur^*guṇe jale[ch:guṇitajalena] pāka ā prakṛty^avasthānāt/ tasya *puṣpa[ch:puṣya]^ārambheṇa prātaḥ prāśanaṃ medhyaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyaṃ yukta^rasam ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/
body.translated_text: 7.1.47. A decoction of <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and the fruits of <s>śrīparṇī</s>, pounded, cooked in four times [as much] water until reduced to its original [one-quarter] state—the morning consumption of this, beginning on [the day of] <s>Puṣya</s>, is beneficial for the intellect, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and of balanced flavor—so they declare.

body.text: 7.1.48/.śvadaṃṣṭrā^cūrṇa^samanvitaṃ tat^samam eva yava^cūrṇaṃ prātar utthāya dvi^*palikam[ch:palakam] anudinaṃ prāśnīyān medhyaṃ vṛṣyam *āyuṣyaṃ[ch omits] yukta^rasam ity *ācakṣate[ch:ācāryāḥ pracakṣate]/ (iti vṛṣyā^yogāḥ/ ekaṣaṣṭitamaṃ prakaraṇam//)(p.367)(p.367)
body.translated_text: 7.1.48. Barley powder mixed with an equal amount of <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> powder—two <s>palas</s> of this consumed daily upon rising in the morning is beneficial for the intellect, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and of balanced flavor—so they declare. (Thus the aphrodisiac preparations. The sixty-first chapter.)

body.text: 7.1.49a/.āyurvedāc ca vedāc ca vidyā^tantrebhya eva ca/(p.367)
body.translated_text: 7.1.49a. From <s>Āyurveda</s>, from the <s>Vedas</s>, and from the treatises of [various] sciences,
7.1.49b. and from trustworthy persons—one should learn the preparations that produce pleasure.
7.1.50a. One should not employ those that are doubtful, or those that endanger the body,
7.1.50b. or those connected with the destruction of life, or those compounded with impure substances.

body.text: 7.1.51a/.*tathā yuktān[ch:tapoyuktaḥ] prayuñjīta śiṣṭair *api na ninditān[ch:anugatān vidhīn]/(p.368)
body.translated_text: 7.1.51a. One should employ those that are properly combined, not condemned even by the learned,
7.1.51b. and those that are welcomed with blessings by Brāhmaṇas and well-wishers.
7.2. Restoration of lost passion, methods of enlargement, and miscellaneous preparations
7.2.1. One who is unable to satisfy a woman of intense passion (<s>caṇḍa-vegā</s>) should employ [these] preparations.

body.text: 7.2.2/.ratasya^upakrame saṃbādhasya kareṇa^upamardanaṃ tasyā rasa^prāpti^kāle ca rata^yojanam iti rāga^pratyānayanam/
body.translated_text: 7.2.2. At the commencement of union, the manual rubbing of the constricted [organ], and the application of union at the time of her reaching [the state of] passion—this is the restoration of passion.

body.text: 7.2.3/.aupariṣṭakaṃ manda^vegasya gatavayaso vyāyatasya śrāntasya ca rāga^pratyānayanam/
body.translated_text: 7.2.3. <s>Aupariṣṭaka</s> (oral congress) is the restoration of passion for one of mild passion, one advanced in age, one who is exercised, and one who is fatigued.
7.2.4. Or one should employ prosthetic devices (<s>apadravya</s>).
7.2.5. Those are made of gold, silver, copper, iron, ivory, buffalo-horn material,

body.text: 7.2.6/.trāpuṣāṇi saisakāni ca mṛdūni śīta^vīryāṇi *vṛṣyāṇi karma^sahiṣṇūni[ch:karmāṇi ca dhṛṣṇūni] bhavanti^iti bābhravīyā yogāḥ/
body.translated_text: 7.2.6. or of tin and lead—[which are] soft, cooling in potency, aphrodisiac, and capable of bearing use—these are the preparations of the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
7.2.7. [They may also be] made of wood, and of proper proportions—so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
7.2.8. The difference in the measure of the organ should be made up with dots (<s>bindu</s>), rough on the surface, in abundance.
7.2.9. These same [two devices together make] a pair (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>).
7.2.10. Three or more, up to the [required] measure, [make] a bracelet (<s>cūḍaka</s>).

body.text: 7.2.11/.ekām eva latikāṃ pramāṇa^vaśena veṣṭayed ity eka^cūḍakaḥ/
body.translated_text: 7.2.11. One who wraps a single creeper according to the [required] measure—that is a single bracelet (<s>ekacūḍaka</s>).

body.text: 7.2.12/.ubhayato^mukha^cchidraḥ sthūla^karkaśa^*pṛṣata[ch:vṛṣaṇa]^guṭikā^yuktaḥ pramāṇa^*yogī[ch:vaśa^yogī] kaṭhyāṃ baddhaḥ kañcuko jālakaṃ vā/
body.translated_text: 7.2.12. Open at both ends, fitted with thick, rough, spherical beads, proportioned to [the required] measure, tied at the waist—[this is] a sheath (<s>kañcuka</s>) or a net (<s>jālaka</s>).

body.text: 7.2.13/.tad^abhāve +alābūnālakaṃ veṇuś ca taila^kaṣāyaiḥ subhāvitaḥ *sūtra^jaṅghā[ch:sūtreṇa^kaṭyām]^baddhaḥ ślakṣṇā kāṣṭha^mālāl vā grathitā bahubhir āmalaka^asthibhiḥ saṃyukta^ity apaviddha^yogāḥ/
body.translated_text: 7.2.13. In the absence of those, a gourd-stalk or a bamboo tube, well-soaked in oil and astringent decoctions, tied to the thigh with a string; or a smooth wooden garland strung with many <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) seeds—these are the preparations for use without piercing.
7.2.14. But there is no use [of devices] by one who is not pierced—[this introduces the next topic].
7.2.15. Among the Southerners, the piercing of the male organ [is performed] in youth, like [the piercing of] the ears.

body.text: 7.2.16/.yuvā tu śastreṇa cchedayitvā yāvad rudhirasya^āgamanaṃ tāvad udake tiṣṭhet/
body.translated_text: 7.2.16. But a young man, having made incisions with a blade until blood flows, should stand in water for that duration.
7.2.17. And for keeping [the hole] clear, on that same night, union is performed with insistence.
7.2.18. Then, cleansing with astringent [washes] every other day.
7.2.19. Binding with pegs of cane and <s>kuṭaja</s> wood, progressively increasing in size, for enlargement.
7.2.20. Cleansing with <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s> (licorice) mixed with honey.
7.2.21. Then one should enlarge [the hole] with a lead-leaf earring. 7.2.22. And one should anoint [it] with <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking-nut) oil—these are the preparations involving piercing.
7.2.23. In that [pierced hole], prosthetic devices of various shapes should be fitted.

body.text: 7.2.24/.vṛttam ekato vṛttam udūkhalakaṃ kusumakaṃ kaṇṭakitaṃ kaṅka^asthi^gaja^*prahārikam[ch:karakam] aṣṭa^*maṇḍalikaṃ[ch:maṇḍalakaṃ] bhramarakaṃ śṛṅgāṭakam anyāni vā^upāyataḥ karmataś ca bahu^karma^sahatā ca^eṣāṃ mṛdu^karka^śatā yathā sātmyam iti naṣṭa^rāga^pratyānayanam/ (*dvāṣaṣṭitamaṃ[ch:dviṣaṣṭitamaṃ] prakaraṇam//)(p.369)
body.translated_text: 7.2.24. Round, round on one side, mortar-shaped, flower-shaped, thorny, heron-bone[-shaped], elephant-trunk[-shaped], eight-ringed, spinning-wheel[-shaped], triangular, and others—according to means and practice; and their softness or roughness [should be adjusted] as suits [the woman]—this is the restoration of lost passion. (The sixty-second chapter.)

body.text: 7.2.25/.evaṃ vṛkṣajānāṃ jantūnaṃ śūkair *upaliptaṃ[ch:upahitaṃ] liṅgaṃ daśarātraṃ tailena mṛditaṃ punaḥ *punar upaliptaṃ[ch:upatṛṃhitaṃ] punaḥ pramṛditam iti jāta^śophaṃ khaṭvāyām adho^mukhas tad antare lambayet/
body.translated_text: 7.2.25. Thus, the organ smeared with the bristles (<s>śūka</s>) of tree-insects, rubbed with oil for ten nights, smeared again and rubbed again—when swelling has arisen, one should hang it downward through a hole in the bed while lying face-down.
7.2.26. Then, having restrained the pain with cooling astringent [applications], one should bring it to completion with [further] treatment.

body.text: 7.2.27/.sa yāvaj jīvaṃ śūkajo nāma śopho viṭānām/
body.translated_text: 7.2.27. That swelling caused by bristles (<s>śūka</s>) lasts for life—[this is the method] of libertines (<s>viṭa</s>).

7.2.28. Rubbing with the juice of <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>śabarakanda</s>, water-bristles, <s>bṛhatī</s>-fruit, buffalo butter, <s>hastikarṇa</s> (elephant-ear plant), or <s>vajravallī</s>—one by one, [for] monthly enlargement.

body.text: 7.2.29/.etair eva kaṣāyaiḥ pakvena tailena parimardanaṃ ṣaṇ^māsyam/
body.translated_text: 7.2.29. Rubbing with oil cooked with these very astringents—[this is done for] six months.

body.text: 7.2.30/.dāḍima^*trapusa[ch:trapuṣa]^bījāni *bālukaṃ[ch:bālukā] bṛhatīphala^rasaś ca^iti mṛdv^agninā pakvena tailena parimardanaṃ pariṣeko vā/
body.translated_text: 7.2.30. Seeds of pomegranate and cucumber, sand, and the juice of <s>bṛhatī</s>-fruit—rubbing or pouring with oil cooked over a gentle fire [with these].

body.text: 7.2.31/.tās tāṃś ca yogān āptebhyo budhyeta^iti vardhana^yogāḥ/ (triṣaṣṭitamaṃ prakaraṇam//)(p.369)
body.translated_text: 7.2.31. And one should learn various [other] preparations from trustworthy persons—these are the preparations for enlargement. (The sixty-third chapter.)
7.2.32. If one sprinkles [a woman] with powders of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) thorns mixed with <s>punarnavā</s>, monkey-dung, and the root of <s>lāṅgalikā</s>—she will not desire another.

body.text: 7.2.33/.tathā somalatā^*avalguja[ch:avalgujā]^bhṛṅga^loha^upajihvikā^cūrṇair vyādhighātaka^jambū^phala^rasa^niryāsena ghanī^kṛtena lipta^saṃbādhāṃ gacchato rāgo naśyati/
body.translated_text: 7.2.33. Likewise, if one goes to a woman whose private parts have been smeared with a paste solidified with the juice of <s>vyādhighātaka</s> and <s>jambū</s> fruit, [mixed with] powders of <s>somalatā</s>, <s>avalguja</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>loha</s>, and <s>upajihvikā</s>—passion is destroyed [for her].
7.2.34. If one goes to a woman who has bathed [in a preparation of] powders of <s>gopālikā</s>, <s>bahupādikā</s>, and <s>jihvikā</s> mixed with buffalo buttermilk—passion [for her] is destroyed.
7.2.35. An ointment prepared with the flowers of <s>nīpa</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, and <s>jambū</s> causes misfortune—and so do garlands [made from these].
7.2.36. An application of <s>kokilākṣa</s> fruit makes a <s>hastinī</s>-type [woman's organ] compact for one night.
7.2.37. Powders of lotus, blue lily, <s>kadamba</s>, <s>sarjaka</s>, and fragrant substances, ground with honey and applied—[this is a method for] widening a <s>mṛgī</s>-type [woman].
7.2.38. <s>Āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) fruits soaked in the milky sap of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>soma</s>-plant, and <s>arka</s>, with <s>avalgujā</s> fruits—[this is for] whitening the hair.
7.2.39. Bathing with the roots of <s>madayantikā</s>, <s>kuṭajaka</s>, <s>añjanikā</s>, <s>girikarṇikā</s>, and <s>ślakṣṇaparṇī</s>—[this is for] the restoration of hair.

body.text: 7.2.40/.etair eva supakvena tailena^abhyaṅgāt kṛṣṇī^*karaṇaṃ[ch:karaṇāt] krameṇa^asya pratyānayanam/
body.translated_text: 7.2.40. By anointing with oil well-cooked with these same [substances]—blackening [of the hair]; by gradual [application]—its restoration.

body.text: 7.2.41/.śvetāśvasya muṣka^svedaiḥ sapta^kṛtvo bhāvitena^alaktakena rakto +adharaḥ śveto bhavati/
body.translated_text: 7.2.41. A lip [made] red with lac that has been soaked seven times in the sweat from the testicles of a white horse becomes white [i.e., returns to its natural color].
7.2.42. <s>Madayantikā</s> and the other [substances mentioned above] are [also used for] restoration [of lip color].

body.text: 7.2.43/.bahupādikā^kuṣṭha^tagara^tālīsa^devadāru^vajrakandakair upaliptaṃ vaṃśaṃ vādayato yā śabdaṃ śṛṇoti sā vaśyā bhavati/
body.translated_text: 7.2.43. She who hears the sound of a bamboo flute that has been smeared with [a paste of] <s>bahupādikā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>tālīsa</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>vajrakandaka</s>, [and] played—she becomes submissive.
7.2.44. Food mixed with <s>dhattūra</s> (thorn-apple) fruit causes madness.
7.2.45. Jaggery, when digested, is the antidote.

body.text: 7.2.46/.haritāla^manaḥśilā^bhakṣiṇo mayūrasya purīṣeṇa lipta^hasto yad dravyaṃ spṛśati tan na dṛśyate/
body.translated_text: 7.2.46. The droppings of a peacock that has eaten <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment) and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar)—whatever object is touched by a hand smeared with these is not seen [i.e., becomes invisible].
7.2.47. Water mixed with the ashes of charcoal-grass and oil becomes milk-colored.

body.text: 7.2.48/.*harītaky[ch:harītaka]^āmrātakayoḥ śravaṇapriyaṃgukābhiś ca piṣṭābhir liptāni loha^bhāṇḍāni tāmrī^bhavanti/
body.translated_text: 7.2.48. Iron vessels coated with ground <s>harītakī</s> and <s>āmrātaka</s> [mixed with ground] <s>śravaṇapriyaṃgukā</s> become copper-colored.

body.text: 7.2.49/.śravaṇapriyaṃgukā^tailena dukūla^sarpa^nirmokeṇa vartyā dīpaṃ prajvālya pārśve dīrghī^kṛtāni kāṣṭhāni sarpavad dṛśyante/
body.translated_text: 7.2.49. If a lamp is lit with a wick [made] from silk-cloth and snake-skin, [soaked in] <s>śravaṇapriyaṃgukā</s>-oil, sticks placed alongside appear like serpents when elongated [by the flickering light].

body.text: 7.2.50/.śvetāyāḥ śveta^vatsāyā goḥ kṣīrasya pānaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam/
body.translated_text: 7.2.50. Drinking the milk of a white cow with a white calf is conducive to fame and long life.

body.text: 7.2.51/.brāhmaṇānāṃ praśastān āmāśiṣaḥ/ (iti citrā yogāḥ/ catuḥṣaṣṭitamaṃ prakaraṇam//)(p.370)
body.translated_text: 7.2.51. The auspicious blessings of Brāhmaṇas are commended. (Thus the miscellaneous preparations. The sixty-fourth chapter.)
7.2.52a. Having surveyed the earlier treatises and having had recourse to [actual] practice,
7.2.52b. this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been carefully set forth in abridged form.

body.text: 7.2.53a/.dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca pratyayaṃ lokam eva ca/(p.370)
body.translated_text: 7.2.53a. One who knows the true meaning of this sees <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, faith, and the ways of the world,

body.text: 7.2.53b/.paśyaty etasya tattvajño na ca rāgāt pravartate//(p.370)
body.translated_text: 7.2.53b. and does not act merely out of passion.
7.2.54a. Those miscellaneous [preparations] that increase passion, mentioned as required by the subject,
7.2.54b. immediately thereafter in this very [text] have been carefully prohibited [from indiscriminate use].

body.text: 7.2.55a/.na śāstram asti^ity etena prayogo hi samīkṣyate/(p.370)
body.translated_text: 7.2.55a. [One should] not [think] 'this is not a science'—for practice is indeed examined [herein].
7.2.55b. One should know that the principles of the science are comprehensive, while practices are [applicable only] in particular cases.
7.2.56a. Having thoroughly considered the sūtra-meanings of [the tradition of] <s>Bābhravya</s> and the received tradition,
7.2.56b. <s>Vātsyāyana</s> composed this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> according to proper method.
7.2.57a. This was composed through supreme celibacy and concentration,
7.2.57b. for the conduct of worldly life—its prescription is not [meant] for the purpose of passion [alone].
7.2.58a. One who knows the true meaning of this science, guarding the proper conduct of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> as it operates in the world,
7.2.58b. becomes indeed one of controlled senses.
7.2.59a. Therefore, a skilled and learned person, observing <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>,
7.2.59b. not being excessively passionate—one who applies [this knowledge] succeeds.
